confirmed.title: Unlimited free scans via open signup — unbounded scrape/LLM cost
confirmed.evidence: libs/auth.ts:41 `emailAndPassword: { enabled: true }` with no requireEmailVerification, no captcha, and no rateLimit config anywhere in the file; billing.service.ts:229-234 grants one free scan to any user row: `.update(user_credits).set({ free_scan_used: true ... }).where(...eq(user_credits.free_scan_used, false))` — every fresh account gets a free scan. The only scan rate limit is per-user (reports.service.ts:216-220), not per-IP.
confirmed.impact: A script can register throwaway accounts in a loop (better-auth's default in-memory limiter is per-process and generous), and each account's free scan fans out to up to 9 platform scrapes (Apify/X API paid providers) plus the full multi-stage LLM synthesis. Attacker-controlled, unbounded provider spend and worker-queue flooding that also starves paying users' scans.
confirmed.fix: Require email verification before granting the free scan (or grant it only after first verified login), add per-IP rate limiting on /v1/auth/* and POST /v1/reports (better-auth rateLimit with DB storage, or a reverse-proxy limit), and add a global concurrency/cost circuit breaker on scan creation.
confirmed.verifierNote:
I tried to refute this and could not. Every load-bearing fact checks out against the code as it actually deploys:

1. **Open signup, no friction** — `auth.ts:41` `emailAndPassword: { enabled: true }` with no `requireEmailVerification`, no captcha/turnstile, no `rateLimit` block anywhere in the file (grep confirmed). The frontend actively exposes it: `web/src/lib/axios.ts` maps `signUp: "/v1/auth/sign-up/email"` and `signin.tsx` has a working signup mode. So `POST /v1/auth/sign-up/email` mints a usable session with zero verification.

2. **Free scan for every account** — `billing.service.ts:222-234`: `consumeCreditForScan` upserts a `user_credits` row (`balance:0, free_scan_used:false`) then atomically flips `free_scan_used false->true` and returns early (no paid debit). Every fresh user row therefore gets exactly one no-cost scan.

3. **The scan is expensive and attacker-shaped** — `reports.service.ts:284-328`: the credit is consumed inside the same tx that inserts the report and enqueues `report_platform_jobs` for `input.selected_platforms` (attacker-controlled). `ENABLED_PLATFORMS` includes 9 platforms, among them `linkedin` and `twitter`, which the repo routes through paid providers (Apify / X API), plus multi-stage LLM synthesis on OpenRouter/Anthropic (real per-token cost). A fresh account with a novel competitor name misses the smart-rescan cache (`findExistingPlatformData`) and fully scrapes + synthesizes.

4. **Only per-user throttle** — `reports.service.ts:216-220`: "max 10 scans per hour" is scoped `eq(reports.owner_id, owner_id)` — per account, not per IP and not global. N throwaway accounts = N free scans; no global concurrency/spend ceiling exists (worker concurrency env vars only pace processing, they don't cap total cost — queued jobs still run and still bill).

Deployment reality doesn't save it. NODE_ENV=production is set (ecosystem.config.cjs), so better-auth's default in-memory rate limiter is active, but there is exactly ONE api PM2 process (`rivaleye-api`), so the limiter is a single per-IP ~100 req/min bucket — trivially bypassed with rotating IPs or a slow drip, and the claim already accounts for it. The create-report handler is `auth: {}` (any authenticated user), so the freshly-registered session clears the only gate. Single VM / PgBouncer pool max 5 bounds throughput, not attacker-controlled provider/LLM spend — jobs simply queue and drain, each incurring cost and starving legitimate paying users' scans.

I downgraded from critical to high: it is a genuine financial-DoS / cost-amplification hole, trivially reachable, but it requires scripted account creation and each account is capped at 10 scans/hr, and a weak per-IP limiter raises the bar slightly — so it is not a single-request instant-catastrophe. Real, and worth fixing before launch (require email verification, add captcha on signup, and/or a global/per-IP scan-enqueue budget).

confirmed.title: Credit balance lost-update: grantCreditsForOrder uses read-modify-write without atomic increment or row lock
confirmed.evidence: billing.service.ts:126-144 — inside the transaction it does `const existing = await trx.select().from(user_credits)...` then `set({ balance: existing[0]!.balance + tx.amount })`. No `FOR UPDATE`, no `sql\`balance + ${amount}\``. Contrast with consumeCreditForScan (line 239) which correctly uses `sql\`${user_credits.balance} - 1\``.
confirmed.impact: Under READ COMMITTED, a concurrent grant (webhook for another order) or a concurrent scan debit that commits between the read and the write is silently overwritten: a paying user can lose an entire purchased pack's credits (or gain back a spent credit). This is a real-money corruption bug that will surface exactly when the Razorpay webhook and browser /verify race — which the code explicitly encourages ("can race freely").
confirmed.fix: Use an atomic SQL increment: `set({ balance: sql`${user_credits.balance} + ${tx.amount}` })` (and an upsert `onConflictDoUpdate` instead of select-then-insert/update), or SELECT ... FOR UPDATE the user_credits row.
confirmed.verifierNote: The non-atomic read-modify-write at packages/api/src/services/billing.service.ts:126-144 is a real lost-update hazard: plain SELECT then set({ balance: existing[0]!.balance + tx.amount }) with no FOR UPDATE and no SQL-level increment, under default READ COMMITTED with a 5-connection pool and concurrent request handling. However, the claim's headline scenario is wrong: the webhook-vs-/verify race for the SAME order cannot lose credits, because grantCreditsForOrder first executes a conditional claim UPDATE on credit_transactions (WHERE razorpay_payment_id IS NULL); the losing transaction blocks on that row lock, re-evaluates the predicate after commit, matches 0 rows, and exits with granted=false before touching user_credits — exactly one balance write happens per order. The races that CAN fire are narrower: (1) grant vs consumeCreditForScan — the debit runs at the top of the report-creation transaction (reports.service.ts:285) which holds the user_credits row lock through report insert and platform-data copies, a realistic tens-to-hundreds-of-ms window; a concurrent grant reading the pre-debit balance overwrites the debit, refunding 1 spent credit (loss to the company, not the user). (2) grant vs grant for two DIFFERENT orders by the same user (e.g., dropped /verify on order 1 whose delayed webhook overlaps order 2's /verify) — this can lose a whole purchased pack, but requires two grant transactions for one user overlapping within milliseconds, an unusual coincidence. Nothing in deployment (PM2 single VM, PgBouncer transaction pooling, postgres-js per-transaction connection pinning) prevents either race, and no isolation-level override or other guard exists. Real bug with a trivial fix (use sql`balance + amount` like line 239 does), but downgraded from critical: the common race is guarded, the plausible manifestation leaks 1 credit in the user's favor, and pack-loss requires a rare double-grant overlap.

confirmed.title: Retry endpoints bypass the credit system with no rate limit — free unlimited scrape + LLM re-runs
confirmed.evidence: retryPlatform (reports.service.ts:658-673) sets `attempt_count: 0` and re-queues a full platform scrape + Stage A/B LLM run; retrySynthesis (lines 720-741) re-queues the entire Stage C→E synthesis chain and deletes checkpoints (lines 749-755) forcing full re-computation. Neither consumeCreditForScan nor the 10-scans/hour check in createReport (line 216-220) applies to these endpoints, and the handlers (retryPlatform.ts, retrySynthesis handler) have no throttling.
confirmed.impact: Any authenticated user (including a free-scan account) can loop POST /v1/reports/:id/retry-platform and /retry-synthesis to re-run paid scraping providers and multi-stage LLM synthesis indefinitely for one credit — unbounded cost, and a trivial way to saturate the single-VM worker so other users' scans stall.
confirmed.fix: Cap total retries per report (e.g. persist a retry_count and refuse after N), rate-limit the retry endpoints per user, and only allow retry when the target job is in a failed/terminal state.
confirmed.verifierNote: Verified, not refuted. (1) Credits/rate-limit exist only in createReport (consumeCreditForScan at reports.service.ts:285, 10/hour check at 215-220); retryPlatform (636-690) and retrySynthesis (692-764) have neither, and their handlers use auth:{} with no throttling; no global rate-limit middleware exists in the API. (2) In the deployed postgres engine, claimSourceJob filters only status='queued', and processSourceJob aborts only for cancelled reports — a completed report's job reset by retryPlatform runs fetchPosts unconditionally (source-worker.ts:166), incurring a real paid provider call (Apify for G2/Capterra/LinkedIn/Gmaps) on every retry; retryPlatform's only guard blocks status='running', so completed jobs are infinitely retryable. (3) retrySynthesis deletes C/D/E checkpoints (749-755), defeating the checkpoint-skip logic in pipeline/run.ts, so each retry re-runs ~8 LLM calls (Stage C merge, Stage D synth + 5 role sections, Stage E refine); its guard only blocks a run locked within 15 min. (4) Job claiming is FIFO by created_at which retries don't update, so an attacker's reset jobs sort ahead of other users' jobs and can starve the single VM's scrape (concurrency 8) and synth (concurrency 2) workers. One correction to the evidence: retryPlatform does NOT re-run Stage A/B LLM when a brief is cached (source-worker.ts:219-229 returns cached extract and skips Stage B) — per-retry LLM cost on that path is zero after the first run; the unbounded LLM cost is on the retrySynthesis path, and the unbounded scrape-provider cost is on the retryPlatform path. Severity: high, not critical — requires an authenticated account owning a report, iterations are serialized per job row, and per-iteration cost is cents; still an unbounded-spend and availability gap exploitable from a single free account.

confirmed.title: Non-atomic read-modify-write of user_credits.balance in credit grant — lost updates corrupt paid balances
confirmed.evidence: grantCreditsForOrder(): `const existing = await trx.select().from(user_credits)...` then `.set({ balance: existing[0]!.balance + tx.amount })`. The balance is computed in app code from a stale read, unlike consumeCreditForScan (line 239) which correctly uses `sql`${user_credits.balance} - 1``. There is also no CHECK (balance >= 0) on user_credits (packages/api/src/db/schema/billing.ts:16-21) as a backstop.
confirmed.impact: Under READ COMMITTED, two concurrent grants for the same user (e.g. webhook `payment.captured` for order A racing browser /verify for order B, or a grant racing a scan debit) both read the same starting balance; the second UPDATE overwrites with a stale-computed value. A user who bought a pack while a scan debited can end up with the debit silently un-done (free credits) or a purchased pack's credits silently lost (paid money, no credits, support escalation).
confirmed.fix: Use an atomic SQL increment: `.set({ balance: sql`${user_credits.balance} + ${tx.amount}` })`, or a single upsert `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (user_id) DO UPDATE SET balance = user_credits.balance + EXCLUDED.balance`. Add `CHECK (balance >= 0)` via a Drizzle migration as a backstop.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed by reading the code. grantCreditsForOrder (billing.service.ts:126-143) computes the new balance in app code from a plain SELECT (`existing[0]!.balance + tx.amount`) inside a default READ COMMITTED transaction (db/client.ts sets no isolation; no FOR UPDATE, no advisory lock, no retry logic anywhere in packages/api/src). Postgres's EvalPlanQual re-check cannot save it because the SET value is a client-side literal. Meanwhile consumeCreditForScan (line 239) uses the atomic `sql`balance - 1`` pattern, so a grant racing a committed debit overwrites it (debit undone = free credit), and two grants for different orders lose one pack (paid credits vanish silently). The idempotency machinery (conditional claim UPDATE + partial unique index on razorpay_payment_id) only serializes competing grants for the SAME order — it does nothing across different orders or grant-vs-debit. The scenario is possible as deployed: a single Bun/Elysia process interleaves webhook, /verify, and report-create requests across await points, and the postgres-js pool (max 5) via PgBouncer runs the transactions concurrently. Also unguarded: the insert branch (line 132-138) has no onConflictDoNothing, so a grant racing the debit's row-creating insert aborts with a PK violation. schema/billing.ts:16-21 confirms no CHECK(balance >= 0) backstop. Severity corrected to medium rather than high/critical: the race window is one SELECT-to-UPDATE transaction span (~tens of ms) and requires two concurrent balance mutations for the same user; the by-far most common concurrent pair (webhook + browser /verify for the same order) is already correctly idempotent, so at MVP traffic this is a rare but real, silent, money-integrity lost-update. Fix is trivial: use sql`${user_credits.balance} + ${tx.amount}` or an upsert with ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE.

confirmed.title: Plaintext session cookies stored at rest in report_pdf_jobs
confirmed.evidence: `session_cookie: text("session_cookie")` on report_pdf_jobs; populated verbatim in enqueuePdfJob (packages/api/src/services/pdf-export-jobs.service.ts:20 `session_cookie: params.sessionCookie || null`). It is cleared only after a successful render or after retries are exhausted (packages/worker/src/pg-runner/pdf-worker.ts:64, 83); a job that sits queued (pdf worker down, backlog) keeps the user's live better-auth session token readable in the table, in logical backups, and in Supabase dashboard/pg_dump output.
confirmed.impact: Any DB read access (leaked backup, compromised Supabase service key, drizzle-studio screen share) yields live session tokens enabling full account takeover of every user who requested a PDF while the queue had depth. Sessions in the sessions table are at least opaque tokens scoped to auth; this duplicates them into an unrelated job table.
confirmed.fix: Do not persist the raw cookie: mint a short-lived single-purpose signed token (JWT with report_id scope, 10 min TTL) for the render fetch instead, or have the worker query the DB directly rather than re-authenticating through HTTP. At minimum encrypt the column with a key held only by api+worker and add a sweeper that nulls session_cookie on any job older than N minutes.
confirmed.verifierNote: Verified end-to-end: exportPdf.ts:24 stores the raw Cookie header (full signed better-auth session token) verbatim via pdf-export-jobs.service.ts:20 into the plaintext text column report_pdf_jobs.session_cookie (pipeline.ts:152). pdf-worker.ts clears it only on success or retry exhaustion; retryable failures re-queue the row with the cookie intact. The PDF poller runs only in the rivaleye-synth PM2 process as a single serial loop, so backlog/downtime windows are realistic in the deployed 5-process setup, and even happy-path rows land in Supabase WAL/backups (UPDATE to null does not scrub dead tuples or PITR history). Refutation attempts failed: better-auth cookies are HMAC-signed with BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, so unlike the sessions table (token without signature), this column is directly replayable — DB read access alone yields account takeover. Downgraded from critical to high because exploitation requires a secondary compromise (backup leak, service-key compromise, or DB dump access) and tokens are bounded by session expiry; it is a stored-credential-at-rest flaw, not a directly reachable exploit.

confirmed.title: No index on reports.owner_id — every list/dashboard/rate-limit query seq-scans the hottest table
confirmed.evidence: The reports pgTable has no index block at all (only the PK). Hot queries filter by owner_id: reports.service.ts:67 (`.where(eq(reports.owner_id, owner_id)).orderBy(desc(reports.created_at))` — list page), :219 (rate-limit count per create), :97-99 (smart-rescan lookup by owner_id + primary_competitor_name + created_at), and dashboard.service.ts:99, 123, 136, 193 fire four more owner_id scans per dashboard load. Confirmed no migration creates any reports index (grep of all CREATE INDEX statements in drizzle/*.sql).
confirmed.impact: At thousands of users the reports table is scanned end-to-end multiple times per page view and once per report creation. With the API pool capped at max 5 behind PgBouncer (db/client.ts:11), a few concurrent dashboard loads at scale saturate the pool with seq scans and stall unrelated requests, including scan creation.
confirmed.fix: Add `index("reports_owner_id_created_at_idx").on(t.owner_id, t.created_at)` (covers list ordering, rate-limit window, and rescan lookup) via `pnpm db:generate`.
confirmed.verifierNote: Fact-checked and confirmed: reports pgTable (schema/reports.ts:41) declares no indexes, no migration in drizzle/*.sql creates any reports index (while outreach_items and report_pdf_jobs DO get owner_id indexes, showing this is an oversight), and every cited hot query (reports.service.ts:67, :97-99, :219; dashboard.service.ts:99, 123, 136, 193) filters on the unindexed owner_id. Pool is max 5 with prepare:false behind PgBouncer (db/client.ts:11). So the defect is real: every list/dashboard/rate-limit query seq-scans reports today, with no guard, and the cost grows unboundedly with data. However, the claimed impact is overstated for the deployment as it exists: an MVP-scale table (hundreds to low-thousands of rows, kept small by the hourly per-user rate limit) seq-scans in sub-millisecond time from cache; TOASTed text/jsonb columns aren't read for filtered-out rows; and postgres.js queues excess queries rather than failing, so the effect at growth is gradual latency, not the described hard stall of scan creation. Downgraded from critical to medium: certain-to-manifest scalability defect on the hottest table, trivially fixed with one Drizzle index migration, but no near-term production failure scenario at current scale.

confirmed.title: 15 report_* child tables have FKs to reports but no report_id index — report page reads, persist deletes, and cascades all seq-scan

confirmed.title: LinkedIn and Twitter scrapers silently return [] on auth failure/login wall — expired session cookies produce permanently empty platforms marked 'completed'
confirmed.evidence: `if (!result.data?.length) { console.warn(`[linkedin] 0 posts for "${query.competitor}"`); return []; }` — same pattern at twitter/index.ts:185-188. Both scrapers authenticate with static session cookies from env (LINKEDIN_LI_AT, LINKEDIN_JSESSIONID, TWITTER_AUTH_TOKEN, TWITTER_CT0, linkedin/index.ts:18-25). When those cookies expire or the account is banned, the headless page lands on a login wall, the DOM selectors match nothing, and the scraper returns an empty array. source-worker.ts:192-217 then marks the job status='completed' with posts_count: 0 and proceeds to fan-in.
confirmed.impact: The day the shared LinkedIn/Twitter session cookies expire (JSESSIONID/ct0 rotate frequently; li_at on password change), every report silently loses those platforms with zero errors, zero retries, and no alert — jobs report 'completed'. Customers get thinner reports and nobody knows until someone manually inspects. Additionally these DOM selectors (`.feed-shared-update-v2`, `article[data-testid="tweet"]`) break silently the same way on any platform HTML change. This also violates the repo's own rule 'Never silently return [] on error. Throw ScraperError.'
confirmed.fix: In the Browserless script, detect the login-wall/authwall state (URL contains /login, /authwall, /i/flow/login, or zero UserCell/article elements after successful navigation) and return an explicit auth_failed flag; map that to a thrown ScraperError (ideally PermanentError) so the job fails loudly and can page an operator. Alert on N consecutive zero-post runs per platform.
confirmed.verifierNote:
Attempted to refute and could not — every link in the claimed failure chain is verified in the code as deployed.

1) Static cookie auth is real: packages/scrapers/src/linkedin/index.ts:17-29 requires LINKEDIN_LI_AT/LINKEDIN_JSESSIONID/LINKEDIN_BCOOKIE; packages/scrapers/src/twitter/index.ts:16-26 requires TWITTER_AUTH_TOKEN/TWITTER_CT0. All are set in the repo's live .env, and both platforms are registered in getScraper (scrapers/src/index.ts:40-43) and listed in ENABLED_PLATFORMS (packages/shared/src/llm/config.ts:11-12), so the path is live in production.

2) Login wall produces [] not an error: both scrapers POST a Browserless /function script that injects cookies, navigates, and runs querySelectorAll ('.feed-shared-update-v2...' / 'article[data-testid="tweet"]'). There is zero login-wall/authwall detection (grep for login/challenge/authwall/logged in both scraper dirs: no hits). With expired cookies the page renders the auth wall, the script completes normally, Browserless returns HTTP 200 with { data: [] }, so the res.ok ScraperError guard (linkedin:111-114, twitter:167-170) never fires. Lines linkedin:118-121 and twitter:185-188 then console.warn and return []. Twitter is worse: its Step 1-3 blocks use bare `catch (_) {}`, swallowing even navigation timeouts.

3) Worker marks it completed: packages/worker/src/pg-runner/source-worker.ts:192-217 — posts.length === 0 → job status='completed', stage='completed', emits scrape.fetch completed with metadata { posts_count: 0 }, calls fanInCheck, returns. No retry (retries only happen in the catch block, and no error is thrown), no failure, no alert. Synthesis proceeds with the platform silently absent.

4) Nothing in the deployment guards it: the empty result is indistinguishable from a legitimately-quiet competitor, so no downstream check can catch it; pipeline_events rows record posts_count:0 but nothing alerts on them. The PM2/PgBouncer topology is irrelevant — the failure needs only one worker process and expired cookies (ct0/JSESSIONID rotate; li_at dies on password change/security checkpoint), which is a when-not-if event for static cookies shared across all customer reports.

5) It violates the package's own hard rule 4 in packages/scrapers/CLAUDE.md: "Never silently return [] on error. Throw ScraperError." (It also violates rule 5, "Hostile platforms = buy... No headless browser farms in this repo," which is context, not the defect itself.)

Severity high rather than critical: no crash, data corruption, or security exposure — reports still generate from the other 7 platforms — but the day the cookies die, two platforms silently vanish from every report for every customer with 'completed' status and zero signal to operators, and the same silent-empty mode fires on any LinkedIn/X DOM change. Detection requires manual inspection, which is exactly the claimed impact.

confirmed.title: LinkedIn/Twitter scrapers ignore the Sonar-resolved linkedinUrl/twitterHandle and guess the company from its name — wrong company's posts can be ingested into customer reports
confirmed.evidence: ScrapeQuery.linkedinUrl / twitterHandle exist only in types.ts (grep shows no scraper consumes them) even though source-worker.ts:376-377 passes them. LinkedIn builds `https://www.linkedin.com/company/${slugify(query.competitor)}/posts/` (linkedin/index.ts:33-34). Twitter's people-search matcher accepts `handle.includes(slug) || slug.includes(handle)` and, when nothing matches, falls back to the FIRST UserCell: `const first = document.querySelector('[data-testid="UserCell"] [dir="ltr"] span'); return first?.innerText...` (twitter/index.ts:96-101).
confirmed.impact: For competitors whose LinkedIn slug differs from the naive slugification (e.g. 'Monday.com' → 'mondaycom' vs actual 'mondaydotcom') or whose name is ambiguous on X, the scraper harvests a different company's posts and replies. These flow through Stage A/B and into the final Competitor Perception Report as if they were about the competitor — silent data corruption of the core product output. The whole point of the discovery step (per its own comment in types.ts: 'so we never accidentally analyse a lookalike app or wrong company') is defeated for these two platforms.
confirmed.fix: Thread query.linkedinUrl and query.twitterHandle into the scrapers: navigate directly to the discovered company URL/handle when present; remove the first-UserCell fallback (return no profile instead); only fall back to name search when discovery returned null, and require an exact-handle or verified-name match.
confirmed.verifierNote: Confirmed end-to-end. ScrapeQuery.linkedinUrl/twitterHandle are declared in packages/scrapers/src/types.ts:40-41 (with a comment saying they exist to avoid analysing the wrong company), populated by Sonar discovery (packages/shared/src/llm/discover.ts), and passed by packages/worker/src/pg-runner/source-worker.ts:376-377 — but grep proves no scraper ever reads them. LinkedInScraper (linkedin/index.ts:33-34) builds linkedin.com/company/<slugify(competitor)>/posts/ from the name alone; TwitterScraper (twitter/index.ts:91-102) does a people-search with a loose includes() matcher and unconditionally falls back to the FIRST UserCell when nothing matches, then ingests that profile's posts and replies. Both platforms are in ENABLED_PLATFORMS (shared/src/llm/config.ts), so this runs on every production report; the bug is deterministic per-scrape logic, unaffected by the PM2/PgBouncer deployment topology. The only downstream mitigation — Stage A LLM 'RELEVANCE FILTER' prompts — cannot catch the collision case, because a wrong company with the same name produces posts that genuinely discuss '${competitor}' by name. Severity is high, not critical: the Monday.com-style slug-mismatch example mostly yields 404/empty pages (silent data loss, not corruption); true wrong-company ingestion requires the naive slug or top X search result to belong to a real same-named entity, which is plausible for generic SaaS names but not universal, and the other seven platforms plus Twitter's mention search still target the correct name.

confirmed.title: App Store / Play Store name-search path has no total-post cap and Stage A fires all LLM batches in parallel — a single job can ingest 1,250+ reviews and launch ~25 concurrent paid LLM calls
confirmed.evidence: DEFAULT_APP_LIMIT = 5 and DEFAULT_REVIEW_PAGES = 5 (appstore/index.ts:12-13); each RSS page returns up to 50 reviews and fetchReviews loops pages 1..5 per app, so 5 apps × 250 = up to 1,250 posts per job. PlayStore: DEFAULT_APP_LIMIT=3 × DEFAULT_REVIEW_NUM=200 = 600 posts (playstore/index.ts:7-8). source-worker.ts:467-498 then splits into BATCH_SIZE=50 batches and runs them ALL via `Promise.all(batches.map(...))` — 25 parallel OpenRouter calls for one appstore job, with no per-report or global spend cap anywhere.
confirmed.impact: Unbounded, spiky LLM cost: a popular competitor name that matches 5 apps produces ~25 simultaneous LLM requests per appstore job; 8 concurrent source jobs can mean 100+ concurrent OpenRouter calls from one process — rate-limit storms (which then fail the job and retry the whole batch set 3×, tripling spend) and unpredictable per-scan cost. Also bloats mentions storage since every review row duplicates the full app object in raw (`raw: { app, review: r }` — app description/releaseNotes repeated 250×).
confirmed.fix: Add a MAX_TOTAL_POSTS cap per platform job (mirror Reddit's MAX_TOTAL_POSTS pattern) and cap name-search to 1–2 best-matching apps. needs_reverify.title: retryPlatform TOCTOU resets a possibly-claimed job to queued → double-processing; also never resets run_after/locked_*
needs_reverify.evidence: reports.service.ts:645-673 — it SELECTs the job, checks `if (job.status === "running") return ...already_running`, then runs an UPDATE to `status: "queued", stage: "scrape", attempt_count: 0 ...` whose WHERE clause is only `(report_id, platform)` — not conditioned on status. The update also omits `run_after`, `locked_at`, `locked_by` (schema pipeline.ts:55-57 shows run_after drives claiming).
needs_reverify.impact: (1) If a worker claims the job (sets status='running') between the SELECT and the UPDATE, the API flips it back to 'queued' while the worker is mid-scrape; a second worker claims it via FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED on 'queued' rows → the same platform runs twice concurrently: duplicate mentions inserted, double Apify/LLM spend, and racing status writes. (2) If a prior failure left run_after in the future, the "retried" job silently sits unclaimed until that timestamp — a wedged retry the user perceives as broken.
needs_reverify.fix: Make the reset a single conditional UPDATE: `... SET status='queued', run_after=now(), locked_at=NULL, locked_by=NULL, attempt_count=0 WHERE report_id=.. AND platform=.. AND status <> 'running' RETURNING id`, and return already_running when 0 rows update.

needs_reverify.title: No timeout around scraper.fetch in source worker; most scrapers make unbounded network calls — one hung platform wedges a concurrency slot for 25 min, then stale recovery double-processes it
needs_reverify.evidence: fetchPosts() calls `const posts = await scraper.fetch({...})` with no timeout or AbortSignal wrapper. Downstream, LinkedIn (packages/scrapers/src/linkedin/index.ts:102) does `fetch(`${BROWSERLESS_BASE}/function?token=${this.token}`)` with no timeout param and no AbortSignal; reddit auth (reddit/auth.ts:34) uses `axios.post(...)` with no timeout (axios default = infinite); producthunt gql fetch, hackernews algoliaSearch, devto apiGet, and appstore lookupApp/searchApps/fetchReviews are all bare `fetch(url)` with no AbortSignal. Only the Apify helper (unused) and Twitter (`&timeout=60000` — server-side only, client fetch still unbounded) bound anything.
needs_reverify.impact: A stalled TCP connection or slow provider holds one of the 8 source-job slots until the 25-minute stale sweep (pg-runner/index.ts:451 sourceJobTimeoutMinutes: 25). Recovery then resets the job to queued while the original execution is still alive in-process, so a second worker re-runs the full scrape + Stage A/B LLM calls concurrently — duplicated paid LLM/provider spend and a report that appears stuck for 25+ minutes. Under a provider brownout, all 8 slots can wedge simultaneously, halting all scraping tenant-wide.
needs_reverify.fix: Wrap fetchPosts in Promise.race with a per-platform timeout budget (e.g. 3–8 min) that rejects and clears the slot; add AbortSignal.timeout to every raw fetch/axios call in scrapers (reddit auth, linkedin, producthunt, hackernews, devto, appstore). Cancel the underlying work on timeout so the original execution cannot race the recovered one.

needs_reverify.title: Unbounded synthesis prompts: full uncapped signal pool JSON-dumped into 8+ LLM calls per scan
needs_reverify.evidence: assemble-signals.ts:122-128: "Pool every per-platform Stage A signal ... WITHOUT the LLM collapse. Each raw signal becomes its own cluster (1:1) ... No semantic merge, no cap". That uncapped pool is then embedded verbatim, pretty-printed, into every synthesis prompt: prompts/cross/synth.ts:74 `${JSON.stringify(merged, null, 2)}` plus ALL notable quotes (synth.ts:62-66 `extracts.flatMap((e) => e.notable_quotes ?? [])`); prompts/cross/refine.ts:34-37 embeds `JSON.stringify(input.merged, null, 2)` AND `JSON.stringify(input.draft, null, 2)`; all 5 role prompts embed the full pool (founder.ts:93, overview.ts:74, product.ts:109, growth.ts:189, marketing.ts:66 — each `JSON.stringify(mergedSignals, null, 2)`); summary-synthesis.ts:96 embeds every platform extract in full. There is zero token counting, truncation, or cap anywhere in the pipeline (no code matches for token budgets), and stage-d-role.ts retries each of the 5 sections up to 3 times with the same full prompt (MAX_SECTION_ATTEMPTS=3, stage-d-role.ts:25).
needs_reverify.impact: Project memory already records 77k-token prompts from this exact assemble path. A large scan (9 platforms x up-to-125 posts each producing uncapped signals + evidence_index of every quote) sends the same ~50-100k-token blob 8+ times (synth + 5 role sections + summary + refine), with role retries multiplying it up to 3x. Beyond the direct cost (~0.8-1.5M prompt tokens per scan on the happy path), a big-enough scan exceeds the model context window, every attempt fails identically (non-transient), the synthesis job burns its 2 attempts and the report is marked failed — the biggest, most valuable scans are the ones that break. Pretty-printing with 2-space indent alone inflates tokens ~20%.
needs_reverify.fix: Add a token budgeter before every synthesis prompt: cap clusters per signal type (e.g. top-N by frequency*severity), cap evidence_index/representative_quotes per cluster, and serialize with JSON.stringify(x) (no indent). Estimate tokens (chars/4) and degrade gracefully (drop lowest-confidence clusters) until under a per-call budget (e.g. 60k). Log final prompt token estimate per stage.

needs_reverify.title: LLM call in API request path with no timeout — report creation can hang indefinitely
needs_reverify.evidence: keyword-expander.ts:31 `const res = await llm.complete({ system: SYSTEM_PROMPT, user, schema: keywordsSchema });` — no LlmCallOptions passed. In shared/src/llm/openrouter.ts:140, `const signal = timeoutMs ? AbortSignal.timeout(timeoutMs) : undefined;` — with no timeoutMs the fetch has NO abort signal, and maxAttempts defaults to 3 with up-to-30s backoffs (openrouter.ts:114, 61-62). Called from the scan-creation flow at packages/api/src/services/reports.service.ts:228 (`keywords = await expandKeywords(getLlm(), ...)` inside a try/catch).
needs_reverify.impact: During an OpenRouter incident where connections accept but never respond (the classic provider-outage mode), every 'create scan' HTTP request hangs forever inside the Elysia handler — the catch at reports.service.ts:234 only helps if the call *fails*, not if it never returns. With thousands of users this wedges API connections/PgBouncer slots and makes scan creation appear totally down, even though a static keyword fallback exists one line away.
needs_reverify.fix: Pass `{ timeoutMs: 10_000, maxAttempts: 1 }` to this call (the fallback `keywords = [competitor]` is acceptable), or move keyword expansion into the worker. Also consider giving OpenRouterClient a default timeout (e.g. 120s) so no call site can ever run unbounded.

needs_reverify.title: No spend tracking, budget caps, or kill switch for LLM usage
needs_reverify.evidence: The client returns usage per call (openrouter.ts:166-169) but nothing aggregates it: Stage A/B tokens land only in report_platform_briefs (source-worker.ts:578-580), Stage C/D/E usage only goes into report_logs JSON meta via log() (run.ts:244-250, logger.ts:30-37). grep for budget/spend/cost across worker+shared finds no budget code. There is no per-report, per-user, or per-day token ceiling, no abort when a report exceeds a cost threshold, and retries/resynthesis (see other findings) re-pay full prompt costs invisibly.
needs_reverify.impact: Unbounded cost under exactly the conditions the launch will produce: spiky load, big scans, schema-failure retry loops, and resynthesis re-runs. A single pathological report (huge signal pool + 3x role retries + a resynthesis per late platform) can silently cost 10-20x a normal scan, and nobody can answer 'what did this scan cost' or 'cap this user' without ad-hoc SQL over report_logs JSON. Nominal cost is ~$0.4-0.7/scan on deepseek-chat but ~$4-6/scan if OPENROUTER_MODEL is ever pointed at a mid-tier model — with no guardrail either way.
needs_reverify.fix: Accumulate usage into a per-report counter (e.g. reports.llm_prompt_tokens/llm_completion_tokens columns updated after each stage), enforce a hard per-report token budget that aborts the pipeline with a PermanentError when exceeded, and emit a daily aggregate metric. OpenRouter also returns cost in its usage accounting API — reconcile daily.

needs_reverify.title: Missing OPENROUTER_MODEL silently degrades all scans to a heavily rate-limited free model
needs_reverify.evidence: config.ts:17-25: `const FALLBACK_LLM_MODEL = "deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash:free"; if (!process.env.OPENROUTER_MODEL) { console.warn(...) } export const LLM_MODEL = process.env.OPENROUTER_MODEL ?? FALLBACK_LLM_MODEL;` — a warn-and-continue at module load, consumed by api, scrape worker, and synth worker (e.g. source-worker.ts:50-53, run.ts:60, reports.service.ts:40).
needs_reverify.impact: A PM2 env slip (the repo's recent history is exactly PATH/env propagation fixes in ecosystem.config.cjs) puts the entire production pipeline on OpenRouter's free tier: every Stage A/B/D/E call starts 429ing, the client retries 3x with <=30s backoff (openrouter.ts:48,61), jobs burn their attempts, and scans fail or crawl — with the only signal a console.warn in a PM2 log file. Silent quality/failure degradation, not a crash.
needs_reverify.fix: In production (NODE_ENV=production), throw at boot when OPENROUTER_MODEL is unset — same pattern as readOpenRouterApiKey() (config.ts:27-31). Keep the free-model fallback for dev only.

needs_reverify.title: Persisted React Query cache leaks previous user's reports to the next account on the same browser
needs_reverify.evidence: app.tsx:86-97 persists every successful query to localStorage except `me`: `shouldDehydrateQuery: (query) => query.state.status === "success" && query.queryKey[0] !== "me"` with `maxAge: QUERY_CACHE_MAX_AGE` (24h, query-client.ts:4). The cache is cleared ONLY on explicit sign-out (app-shell.tsx:230-232 and account.tsx:58-59 call clearQueryCache()). SignInPage (routes/signin.tsx:64-93) never clears the query cache on sign-in, and query keys are not user-scoped (e.g. reportsKeys.list() = ["reports","list"], use-reports.ts:59-70).
needs_reverify.impact: If user A's session expires (or the tab is closed without signing out) and user B signs in on the same browser, B's session hydrates A's persisted cache: reports list, report detail/sections, competitors, and billing transactions (which include user_id, razorpay ids — api/billing.ts:19-29). With defaultOptions staleTime 10 min (query-client.ts:9), hydrated data is served without any refetch, so B can browse A's full report content entirely from cache. Cross-account data exposure on shared/team machines.
needs_reverify.fix: Clear the query cache and persisted client on successful sign-in/sign-up (call clearQueryCache() in SignInPage before navigate), or include the authenticated user id in the persister key / every query key, or drop localStorage persistence for user-scoped data.

needs_reverify.title: Completed report with missing sections wedges on 'GENERATING ANALYSIS' — promised auto-refresh does not exist
needs_reverify.evidence: scan-report.tsx:303-313: comment says "the refetchInterval above will retry automatically every 5 seconds", and StuckAnalysisState (scan-report.tsx:1734) renders "This usually takes 30–60 seconds. The page will update automatically." But useReportSectionsQuery (hooks/queries/use-report-sections.ts:5-15) has `retry: 0`, `staleTime: 10 * 60 * 1000` and NO refetchInterval. Meanwhile useReportQuery stops polling once status is terminal (use-reports.ts:103-107, TERMINAL_STATUSES includes "completed").
needs_reverify.impact: When a report row reaches status=completed before the LLM sections are written (a normal race under LLM slowness/load), the user sees a static 'AI analysis is being written… page will update automatically' screen that never updates. Because the null-sections result is cached with 10-min staleTime AND persisted to localStorage, even a page reload within 10 minutes re-renders the stuck screen from cache. Scans appear wedged/lost to the user; after 10 minutes the UI pushes them toward 'Retry analysis' / rescans, burning worker+LLM cost for reports that actually finished.
needs_reverify.fix: Give the sections query a refetchInterval while the report is completed but all sections are null (and stop once any section arrives), or keep report status non-terminal until sections are written; at minimum mark the null-sections response as non-cacheable (staleTime 0, don't persist).

genuinely_refuted.title: Scrapers never throw PermanentError/RateLimitError — the worker's retryable-vs-permanent classification is dead code, so permanent failures (missing tokens, 401/403, not-implemented platforms) burn 3 retries and ~7.5 min of backoff per platform per report
genuinely_refuted.evidence: `const isPermanent = err instanceof PermanentError;` and `err instanceof RateLimitError` (source-worker.ts:290-296) — but grep across packages/scrapers/src shows zero imports of PermanentError/RateLimitError; every scraper throws ScraperError or plain Error (e.g. RedditScraper constructor throws ScraperError for missing REDDIT_CLIENT_ID; LinkedInScraper constructor throws plain Error 'BROWSERLESS_TOKEN is required' at linkedin/index.ts:19; G2/Capterra/Trustpilot/Gmaps throw ScraperError 'not implemented'). ScraperError (scrapers/src/types.ts:49) carries no retryable flag.
genuinely_refuted.impact: Any deterministic failure — missing env var after a deploy, revoked API token (401), Sonar-resolved app ID that 404s, a platform accidentally enabled without an implementation — is retried 3 times with 30s/2m/5m backoff (getBackoffMs, source-worker.ts:105-108). Every affected report's fan-in is delayed ~8 minutes and paid provider/Browserless calls are repeated pointlessly. Provider 429s never take the RateLimitError retry-after path, so rate-limit storms use the generic short backoff and hammer the provider again.
genuinely_refuted.fix: Add a `retryable` (or kind: 'permanent' | 'rate_limit' | 'transient') field to ScraperError and set it at each throw site (constructor/env errors, 401/403/404 → permanent; 429 → rate_limit with retryAfterMs; 5xx/network → transient). Map it to PermanentError/RateLimitError in fetchPosts, or have scrapers import the worker error types via shared.
genuinely_refuted.verifierNote: The claim's premise is half-true but its impact is impossible in production. True part: scrapers only throw ScraperError/plain Error (grep of packages/scrapers/src shows zero PermanentError/RateLimitError usage), and the live pg-runner path (pipeline/stage-a-extract.ts, stage-b-summarize.ts) never throws them either — the files that do (worker/src/llm/stage-a.ts, scrape/fetch.ts) are the legacy Inngest path. So the instanceof branches at source-worker.ts:290-296 are inert. Refuted part (the entire claimed impact): every source job is inserted with max_attempts: 1 at the only production insertion point (packages/api/src/services/reports.service.ts:319-338, both postgres and inngest branches), with an explicit comment 'No retries: a failed platform is final and the report proceeds with whatever platforms succeeded, instead of retrying and stalling.' The schema default of 3 is overridden; the max_attempts: 3 at line 739 belongs to synthesis_jobs, and pipeline-jobs.service.ts:createPlatformJobs has no non-test callers. claim.ts:76 increments attempt_count to 1 on claim, so on any failure canRetry = attempt_count(1) < max_attempts(1) = false: the job fails immediately, no backoff ever fires, fanInCheck runs right away (source-worker.ts:348), and the report proceeds with partial data. Therefore no '3 retries / ~7.5 min backoff / ~8 min fan-in delay / repeated paid provider calls' can occur — deterministic failures (missing token, 401, not-implemented) cost exactly one attempt. Also, the not-implemented platforms (g2/capterra/trustpilot/gmaps) are not in ENABLED_PLATFORMS (shared/src/llm/config.ts). What remains is a dead-code cleanup nit (unreachable retry classification and RateLimitError path), not the reported defect; the misclassification is harmless because the retry branch itself is unreachable for source jobs.

genuinely_refuted.title: Reddit: shared 55/min process-wide limiter vs ~130 API calls per job means concurrent Reddit-heavy scans exceed the 25-min stale timeout and get double-processed; 429 sleep is unbounded
genuinely_refuted.evidence: `const limiter = new RateLimiter(55);` is module-level (one bucket per process). Each Reddit job issues up to 5 searches + 125 getComments calls (reddit/index.ts: MAX_SEARCH_TERMS=5, MAX_POSTS_PER_TERM=25, one getComments per post) ≈ 130 calls ≈ 2.4 min solo. With MAX_CONCURRENT_SOURCE=8 (pg-runner/index.ts:55) several concurrent Reddit jobs serialize behind the same bucket: 8 jobs ≈ 1040 calls ≈ 19 min each, and any 429 adds `await sleep(retryAfter * 1000)` (client.ts:44-46) with no cap on the server-supplied retry-after.
genuinely_refuted.impact: Under a signup spike, Reddit jobs routinely approach or exceed the 25-minute sourceJobTimeoutMinutes; recoverStaleJobs resets them to queued while the original execution is still running, producing concurrent duplicate scrapes (double Reddit quota burn, duplicate Stage A/B LLM spend — mentions rows are deduped by the unique index but LLM calls are not). A single hostile retry-after header (e.g. 3600) wedges the job slot for an hour.
genuinely_refuted.fix: Cap retry-after sleeps (e.g. min(retryAfter, 120s), fail the attempt beyond that with a RateLimitError so the job re-queues with run_after instead of sleeping in-process). Reduce per-job comment fetches (fetch comments only for posts that pass the relevance filter — currently comments are fetched before filtering, wasting calls on posts that get discarded at index.ts relevance step). Track expected job duration vs stale timeout, or heartbeat locked_at during long scrapes so recovery doesn't fire on live jobs.
genuinely_refuted.verifierNote: The evidence's individual facts check out (module-level 55/min limiter at client.ts:8; up to ~130 calls/job; MAX_CONCURRENT_SOURCE=8; recovery re-queues at 25 min based on never-refreshed locked_at), but the failure scenario cannot occur as deployed. Production runs exactly ONE scrape process (ecosystem.config.cjs has a single rivaleye-scrape app, no clustering), so the worst case is the claim's own number: 8 concurrent Reddit jobs = ~1040 calls = ~19 min, which is UNDER the 25-min timeout — exceeding it would need >=11 concurrent Reddit jobs, impossible with the 8-slot cap. The 130-call figure is also a ceiling: all 5 search templates contain the competitor name, so seenIds dedup across terms cuts getComments volume, and the initial 55-token burst absorbs spike onset. The LLM tail is deliberately bounded (Stage A/B calls use timeoutMs:90_000, maxAttempts:2 — source-worker.ts:487-489 explicitly comments this exists so a hung call 'can't wedge the job... until the 25-min stale sweep'), so reaching 25+ min needs every component simultaneously at absolute maximum, not 'routine' spike behavior. The 429/unbounded-sleep leg is speculative: one process at 55/min sits well under Reddit's ~100 QPM OAuth budget so 429s should essentially never fire; if one does, retries cap at 3 per call, the retry-after header comes from Reddit's own API (not attacker-controlled, typically seconds), and the scraper swallows per-term/per-post failures anyway. Finally, double-processing damage is already guarded: mentions dedupe, completion updates are guarded with status NOT IN ('completed','cancelled') (source-worker.ts:318,343), and the report_platform_briefs cache makes a duplicate skip Stage A/B if the original persisted first — duplicate LLM spend requires precise overlap inside Stage A. What survives is hardening advice (cap retry-after sleep, heartbeat locked_at during long jobs, max_attempts check in pg-runner/index.ts's local recoverStaleJobs), which is low severity, not the claimed high-impact production defect.

unverified_med_low.title: report_pdf_jobs has no stale-job recovery — a crash mid-render wedges the export as 'running' forever
unverified_med_low.evidence: claimPdfJob only selects `status = 'queued'` (pdf-worker.ts:28), and the recovery loop sweeps only report_platform_jobs and synthesis_jobs (index.ts:297–305, 345–353; recovery.ts likewise). Nothing resets a report_pdf_jobs row stuck in 'running'. Puppeteer launches a full Chrome per job (pdf/render.ts:34) under a synth process with `max_memory_restart: '1500M'` (ecosystem.config.cjs:74), making mid-render kills likely. Jobs are also processed strictly serially (`await processPdfJob(job)` in the loop, pdf-worker.ts:111).
unverified_med_low.impact: Any worker crash/restart during a render (up to ~90s per attempt) leaves that PDF job 'running' forever; the user's export never completes and polling never resolves. The unique work also blocks nothing else, so it fails silently. Serial processing additionally means one slow render queues all other users' exports behind it.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add report_pdf_jobs to the stale sweep (e.g. 5-min timeout, retry up to max_attempts then failed). Consider a small concurrency (2) and a shared browser instance per process instead of a fresh Chrome per job.

unverified_med_low.title: pipeline_events insert is load-bearing: an emit() failure fails the job or blocks its retry transition
unverified_med_low.evidence: `await db.insert(pipeline_events).values(row);` (emit.ts:30) has no try/catch, and every call site awaits it unprotected: job start (source-worker.ts:149), completion (source-worker.ts:247), and crucially inside the catch block *before* the retry/fail status update (source-worker.ts:279–287; synthesis-worker.ts:283–290).
unverified_med_low.impact: A transient DB blip on an observability write: (a) at step 1 throws into the catch and burns one of the job's 3 attempts for no real failure; (b) inside the catch path prevents the `status → queued/failed` transition entirely, leaving the job locked as 'running' until the 25/90-min stale sweep. Telemetry outages thus convert directly into wedged/failed scans.
unverified_med_low.fix: Make emit() best-effort (catch + log, like logger.ts does), or at minimum wrap the emit calls inside catch blocks so the status transition always executes.

unverified_med_low.title: Retry budgets cannot survive a short LLM-provider outage: synthesis gets 2 total runs, source jobs ~7.5 min of backoff, then permanent report failure
unverified_med_low.evidence: Synthesis jobs are created with `max_attempts: 2` (fan-in.ts:98); claim pre-increments attempt_count (claim.ts:156) and retry requires `attempt_count < max_attempts` (synthesis-worker.ts:295) — so exactly 2 runs, with a single 30s–2m backoff between them, after which the report itself is marked failed (synthesis-worker.ts:344–352). Source jobs: max_attempts 3 (pipeline.ts:58) with backoffs 30s/2m/5m (source-worker.ts:105–108). There is no provider-outage detection, circuit breaker, or queue pause anywhere in pg-runner.
unverified_med_low.impact: An OpenRouter/provider outage of ~5–10 minutes permanently fails every in-flight synthesis (throwing away the full scrape + Stage A/B spend for those reports) and permanently fails source platforms across all active scans. At 'thousands of users, spiky load' scale, routine provider incidents translate into batches of dead reports needing manual resurrection.
unverified_med_low.fix: Raise synthesis max_attempts (retries are cheap — C/D/E are checkpointed in report_pipeline_checkpoints) and use longer/jittered backoff ceilings (e.g. up to 30–60 min). Classify provider 5xx/timeout as RateLimitError with retry-after so backoff scales with the outage rather than burning attempts.

unverified_med_low.title: Unbounded parallel LLM fan-out: Stage A runs all batches via Promise.all with no global concurrency limit
unverified_med_low.evidence: `const batchResults = await Promise.all(batches.map(async (batch, ...) => runStageAExtract(...)))` (source-worker.ts:476–498) launches one LLM call per 50-post batch simultaneously. With MAX_CONCURRENT_SOURCE=8 (index.ts:55) and e.g. 250–500 posts per platform, a single scrape process fires 8 × 5–10 = 40–80 concurrent OpenRouter requests, plus synthesis-side calls; there is no shared limiter or token-bucket across jobs.
unverified_med_low.impact: Spiky scans trigger provider rate-limit storms; the resulting 429s/timeouts consume the small per-job attempt budgets (previous finding) and fail platforms, while also spiking cost. Failure of any one batch fails the whole Stage A step and re-runs all batches on retry (briefs are only cached after Stage B persists, source-worker.ts:571–591), multiplying spend.
unverified_med_low.fix: Introduce a process-wide LLM concurrency limiter (simple semaphore in the OpenRouterClient) and use Promise.allSettled with per-batch retry, persisting partial Stage A output so retries don't re-pay completed batches.

unverified_med_low.title: healOrphanedReports runs an unfiltered GROUP BY over all of report_platform_jobs every 30s from two processes
unverified_med_low.evidence: `SELECT rpj.report_id FROM report_platform_jobs rpj GROUP BY rpj.report_id HAVING ... NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM synthesis_jobs ...)` (recovery.ts:230–239) has no created_at/report-status filter, and it is called every 30s from the recovery loop of both the scrape and synth processes (index.ts:390 in each entrypoint's loop). Rows are never archived/deleted.
unverified_med_low.impact: The scan cost grows linearly with all-time scan volume (thousands of users × N platforms per report). On PgBouncer with a small pool this becomes a recurring multi-hundred-ms query every 30s ×2, competing with claim transactions — degraded queue latency and DB load that only ever gets worse.
unverified_med_low.fix: Bound the sweep to recent, non-terminal reports (join reports where status IN ('running','pending') or created_at > now() - interval '7 days') and run it in only one process (or on a slower cadence).

unverified_med_low.title: User session cookies stored in plaintext in report_pdf_jobs; generated PDFs retained in the table indefinitely
unverified_med_low.evidence: `session_cookie: text("session_cookie")` (pipeline.ts:152) holds the requester's full better-auth session cookie in plaintext while the job is queued/running/retrying; it is only nulled on completion or after retries are exhausted (pdf-worker.ts:57, 63–65, 83). `pdf_base64` (pipeline.ts:153) is written on completion and nothing ever deletes it — no `delete(report_pdf_jobs)` exists anywhere in the repo (grep confirmed); exportPdf.ts only reads it.
unverified_med_low.impact: Anyone with DB read access (dump, leaked backup, compromised dashboard) can hijack live user sessions from queued/failed PDF jobs — a security breach vector. Base64 PDFs (~33% inflated, potentially MBs each) accumulate forever in a hot table, bloating storage/backups and slowing the pdf claim index scans.
unverified_med_low.fix: Replace the forwarded cookie with a short-lived single-purpose signed token the export page accepts; if the cookie must be stored, encrypt it and add a TTL sweep. Add a cleanup job deleting completed/failed pdf rows (or nulling pdf_base64) after e.g. 24h.

unverified_med_low.title: No backpressure or queue-depth observability: unlimited accepted scans, single scrape process, and no metrics on queue age/depth or recovery actions
unverified_med_low.evidence: Total scrape throughput is one PM2 process (ecosystem.config.cjs:53) × MAX_CONCURRENT_SOURCE=8 (index.ts:55); synthesis is one process × 2 (index.ts:56). The API inserts platform jobs per scan with no queue-depth gating (api/src/services/reports.service.ts:308–333). Nothing measures or exports queued-job count, oldest-queued age, or recovery/failure counts — the recovery loop logs only to stdout via pino/console (index.ts:328–336; recovery.ts:60,73 use console.log) with no pipeline_events or metrics emission.
unverified_med_low.impact: A spike of 100 scans ≈ 600–900 source jobs at 8-way concurrency (each minutes long, plus Stage A/B LLM) = many hours of FIFO latency; later users' scans silently sit 'queued' with no operator signal, no alerting on rising recovery/failed rates, and no basis for autoscaling. Wedge/regression states (findings above) are discoverable only by reading VM logs.
unverified_med_low.fix: Expose queue gauges (count + max age per status per table) via the existing /health endpoint or a metrics endpoint, alert on thresholds, emit pipeline_events for recovery actions, and cap per-user concurrent scans at enqueue time. Make worker replica count a deploy-time knob (worker ID scheme already supports multiple processes).

unverified_med_low.title: Cancellation is only observed at job start — a cancel during a long scrape or synthesis keeps spending until completion
unverified_med_low.evidence: The cancelled check happens once before processing (`const [reportCheck] = await db.select({ status: reports.status })...` source-worker.ts:131–144; synthesis-worker.ts:63–76). After that, multi-minute scraper calls and dozens of LLM calls (Stage A batches, C/D/E pipeline) run to completion regardless; only the final status writes are guarded with `ne(status,'cancelled')`.
unverified_med_low.impact: A user cancelling a scan seconds after it is claimed still incurs the full Apify + LLM cost for every platform already claimed, and for the synthesis if it started. At scale this is a real cost-control leak, though results are correctly discarded.
unverified_med_low.fix: Re-check report status between expensive phases (after scrape, between Stage A batches, between C/D/E stages) and abort with a cancelled transition.

unverified_med_low.title: Fixed 500ms poll interval across 5+ loops with no jitter or adaptive idle backoff
unverified_med_low.evidence: `pollIntervalMs: 500` (index.ts:450, 485, 507) drives the source, synthesis, and pdf loops; each idle poll is a full claim transaction (BEGIN + SELECT...FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED + COMMIT for source/synth via db.transaction at index.ts:102, pdf-worker.ts:24). Two worker processes therefore issue ~6–8 claim transactions/sec against the PgBouncer pool around the clock even when the queue is empty, all phase-aligned with no jitter.
unverified_med_low.impact: Constant background transaction load on a small pool (competing with the 30s recovery sweeps and real work), amplified linearly if worker processes are ever scaled out. Not a correctness problem, but wasted DB round-trips and PgBouncer churn 24/7.
unverified_med_low.fix: Back off to 2–5s (with jitter) after consecutive empty polls and snap back to fast polling after a successful claim; or use Postgres LISTEN/NOTIFY from the API's job insert to wake pollers.

unverified_med_low.title: Blocking LLM call in POST /v1/reports request path; result is discarded in the default postgres engine
unverified_med_low.evidence: reports.service.ts:227-236 awaits `expandKeywords(getLlm(), ...)` (an OpenRouter chat completion, keyword-expander.ts:31) synchronously inside createReport before any DB write. The `keywords` variable is only used in the `engine === "inngest"` branch (line 350); in the default engine (config/engine.ts:6 defaults to "postgres") it is never persisted or passed to the worker.
unverified_med_low.impact: Every report creation pays a full LLM round-trip of latency (seconds; unbounded if OpenRouter hangs — the catch only fires on rejection, not on a stalled connection) and OpenRouter token cost for output that is thrown away in production. During an LLM-provider slowdown, all scan-creation requests pile up holding Bun request handlers, exactly at spike time. Also violates the repo's own 'api never runs LLM calls' rule.
unverified_med_low.fix: Delete the expandKeywords call from the API path in postgres mode (let the worker expand keywords as part of the scrape job), or at minimum gate it behind `engine === "inngest"` and give the OpenRouter client a hard timeout.

unverified_med_low.title: User session cookies persisted in plaintext in report_pdf_jobs.session_cookie
unverified_med_low.evidence: pipeline.ts:152 `session_cookie: text("session_cookie"), // transient; cleared once rendered`; populated from the raw request Cookie header in exportPdf.ts:24 `sessionCookie: headers["cookie"] || ""` and stored verbatim by pdf-export-jobs.service.ts:20.
unverified_med_low.impact: Live better-auth session tokens (valid ~days) sit at rest in Postgres — exposed to anyone with DB access, Supabase backups, drizzle-studio sessions, or a SQL-injection anywhere in the app. The 'cleared once rendered' promise doesn't cover jobs stuck in queued/failed states, so tokens can persist indefinitely. Compromise yields full account takeover for every user who exported a PDF.
unverified_med_low.fix: Don't ship the user's cookie to the worker: mint a short-lived single-purpose signed token (e.g. @elysiajs/jwt, 5-min TTL, scoped to report_id) for the export view, or have the worker read report data directly from the DB. If the cookie must be stored, encrypt it and add a TTL sweep that nulls the column on all terminal/stale jobs.

unverified_med_low.title: exportPdf enqueues jobs without verifying report ownership and without any rate limit
unverified_med_low.evidence: enqueuePdfJob (pdf-export-jobs.service.ts:8-25) inserts `{ report_id: params.reportId, owner_id: params.ownerId, ... }` with no assertReportOwned call — unlike every reports.service getter. The handler (exportPdf.ts:16-37) passes params.id straight through and declares `auth: { permissions: ["REPORTS_VIEW"] }`, but the auth macro (plugins/auth.ts:13-24) explicitly does not enforce permissions.
unverified_med_low.impact: Any authenticated user can enqueue PDF-export jobs for any other user's report UUID (FK only requires existence), and can spam unlimited enqueues. Each job spins up headless Chrome on the single worker VM — a cheap DoS on the render queue and a UUID-existence oracle (FK violation vs success). Whether cross-tenant data leaks depends entirely on the worker's render view honoring auth — no defense in the API layer.
unverified_med_low.fix: Call assertReportOwned(reportId, ownerId) before insert, and cap queued jobs per user (e.g. reject when an unfinished job already exists for the same report+lens).

unverified_med_low.title: ~40 handlers return raw internal error messages (Postgres, Razorpay) to clients
unverified_med_low.evidence: createReport.ts:22-25 `return status(400, { message: "Failed to create report", error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) })` — the pattern appears in 40 handler files (grep 'e instanceof Error ? e.message' = 40). createOrder.ts:15-17 goes further, putting e.message into `message`, which for Razorpay failures is `Razorpay order creation failed: 400 {raw razorpay body}` (billing.service.ts:74) and for missing config is 'RAZORPAY_KEY_ID and RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET are required' (billing.service.ts:15).
unverified_med_low.impact: Database constraint names, Drizzle/postgres error text, third-party API responses, and configuration state leak to any authenticated caller — reconnaissance material (schema/table names, FK names usable as existence oracles, provider details) and unprofessional error UX in production.
unverified_med_low.fix: Map errors to stable codes at the boundary: log the full error server-side (already done via log.error) and return a generic code/message; only surface messages from an explicit whitelist of typed domain errors (PaymentRequiredError-style).

unverified_med_low.title: retrySynthesis can double-run synthesis that is genuinely still in flight (>15 min LLM stages)
unverified_med_low.evidence: reports.service.ts:710-731 — a 'running' synthesis job whose locked_at is older than 15 minutes is force-reset to queued (`locked_at: null, locked_by: null, attempt_count: 0`) and checkpoints C/D/E are deleted (lines 749-755), while the original worker may still be executing (the multi-stage synthesis with 77k-token prompts can legitimately exceed 15 min under LLM slowness).
unverified_med_low.impact: Two workers synthesize the same report concurrently: duplicate report_complaints/quotes/sections rows or interleaved partial writes, and the checkpoint deletion yanks state from under the in-flight run. Same class of race the pipeline just had fixed on the worker side, reintroduced via the API.
unverified_med_low.fix: Coordinate through the queue instead of force-resetting: set `rerun_requested = true` (the column exists, pipeline.ts:95) and let the worker's own stalled-job reaper reclaim genuinely dead jobs; or raise the threshold well above the worst-case synthesis duration and make the reset UPDATE conditional on locked_at unchanged.

unverified_med_low.title: cancelReport overwrites completed platform-job statuses, destroying reuse data
unverified_med_low.evidence: reports.service.ts:777-780 `await tx.update(report_platform_jobs).set({ status: "cancelled" }).where(eq(report_platform_jobs.report_id, reportId))` — unconditional, flips 'completed' jobs to 'cancelled' too.
unverified_med_low.impact: Smart rescan (findExistingPlatformData, line 128 requires status='completed') and resume-from-report (line 267-269) can no longer see platforms that finished successfully before the cancel — the user re-pays scrape/LLM cost for data already in the DB, and progress UI misreports platforms that actually completed.
unverified_med_low.fix: Scope the update: `WHERE report_id = .. AND status IN ('queued','running')`.

unverified_med_low.title: Bulk mention copy runs inside the createReport transaction in the request path
unverified_med_low.evidence: reports.service.ts:284-315 — inside `db.transaction`, the loop `for (const { platform, reportId } of existingData) { await copyPlatformDataFromPreviousScan(...) }` SELECTs all mentions per platform and re-INSERTs them (copyPlatformDataFromPreviousScan, lines 187-204) — potentially thousands of rows across up to 9 platforms — plus, in inngest mode, an external HTTP call `inngest.send` at line 342 inside the same transaction.
unverified_med_low.impact: A single POST /v1/reports can hold one of the 5 pooled PgBouncer connections for a long multi-statement transaction (and, in inngest mode, for the duration of an external HTTP call). A handful of concurrent 'smart rescan' creations exhausts the pool, stalling every other request including /health — which then falsely reports DB trouble. Ghost jobs are also possible if inngest.send succeeds but the transaction later rolls back... (send-then-rollback leaves queued events pointing at a nonexistent report).
unverified_med_low.fix: Copy mentions with a single `INSERT ... SELECT` server-side statement (no round-tripping rows through the API), or move the copy into the worker as part of the job; move inngest.send after commit.

unverified_med_low.title: /health runs unindexed full-table max() aggregates on both job tables, unauthenticated
unverified_med_low.evidence: server.ts:54-80 getMostRecentWorkerActivityMs selects `max(locked_at), max(completed_at)` from report_platform_jobs and synthesis_jobs with no WHERE. Schema (pipeline.ts:67, 103) only has partial indexes on locked_at `WHERE status='running'`, and no index on completed_at — so both maxes are sequential scans. The endpoint is public (mounted before controllers, no auth).
unverified_med_low.impact: Every health probe (PM2/load-balancer, typically every few seconds) triggers two full table scans that grow linearly with total historical jobs — at thousands of users this becomes a constant, self-inflicted DB load and slows the very pool the probe shares (max 5). Being unauthenticated, it's also a free DB-load amplifier and leaks queue-depth intel to anyone.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add plain btree indexes on locked_at and completed_at (or track 'last worker heartbeat' in a single-row table the worker updates), and cache the queue computation for ~30s in-process; optionally keep /health's body minimal for unauthenticated callers.

unverified_med_low.title: No index on reports.owner_id despite every hot query filtering on it
unverified_med_low.evidence: reports table (reports.ts:41-82) declares no indexes at all; owner_id (line 43) is also nullable. It is the filter for listReports (reports.service.ts:67), the per-user rate-limit count on every createReport (line 219), findExistingPlatformData (line 97), and dashboard queries (dashboard.service.ts:99, 137). listReports and the dashboard recent_reports query (dashboard.service.ts:124-137) also have no LIMIT.
unverified_med_low.impact: As the reports table grows into the tens of thousands, every report-list page load, every dashboard load (which fires 10 parallel queries against a 5-connection pool), and every scan creation does a sequential scan — compounding pool pressure on the shared PgBouncer pool and inflating p99 latency across the whole API.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add `index("reports_owner_id_created_at_idx").on(owner_id, created_at)` via a Drizzle migration, make owner_id NOT NULL, and add LIMIT/pagination to listReports and dashboard recent_reports.

unverified_med_low.title: Scan rate limit is a non-atomic count-then-insert and returns 400 instead of 429
unverified_med_low.evidence: reports.service.ts:216-220 counts recent reports outside the transaction, then the insert happens later inside `db.transaction` (line 284). The thrown generic Error surfaces as HTTP 400 'Rate limit exceeded: max 10 scans per hour' via createReport.ts:22-25.
unverified_med_low.impact: N concurrent requests all read count=9 and all pass — burst overshoot of the cap (bounded in practice by credits, but the free-scan path plus retries make it real). Clients also can't distinguish rate limiting (should be 429 with Retry-After) from validation failure.
unverified_med_low.fix: Enforce the cap inside the transaction (e.g. count with the insert, or an advisory lock per user) and return a typed RateLimitError mapped to 429.

unverified_med_low.title: verifyPayment compares Razorpay HMAC with non-timing-safe string equality
unverified_med_low.evidence: billing.service.ts:157-160 `if (expected !== razorpay_signature) throw new Error("Invalid payment signature")` — while the webhook path correctly uses timingSafeEqual (lines 194-197).
unverified_med_low.impact: Timing side-channel on signature comparison for the browser /verify path. Practical exploitability is low (attacker must forge an HMAC over known ids and can observe only coarse HTTP timing), but it's an inconsistency with the hardened webhook path guarding the same money flow.
unverified_med_low.fix: Use the same length-check + crypto.timingSafeEqual pattern as handleRazorpayWebhook.

unverified_med_low.title: outreach/planned-actions accept arbitrary report_id without ownership check — cross-tenant FK references and UUID oracle
unverified_med_low.evidence: addOutreach (outreach.service.ts:29-44) and addPlannedAction (planned-actions.service.ts:15-26) insert body-supplied report_id with only owner_id stamped from the session — no assertReportOwned. FKs exist (outreach.ts:19, planned-actions.ts:10). Handler catch blocks return raw e.message (addOutreach handler follows the same leak pattern), so an FK violation reads differently from success.
unverified_med_low.impact: User A can attach outreach/planned-action rows to user B's report: (a) probing which report UUIDs exist (FK error vs success), (b) A's rows are silently cascade-deleted when B deletes their report. No cross-tenant read, since listings are owner-scoped.
unverified_med_low.fix: Verify the report belongs to the caller (assertReportOwned) before inserting in both services.

unverified_med_low.title: Seed script truncates users and all report tables with no environment guard
unverified_med_low.evidence: seed.ts:43+ `TRUNCATE TABLE report_thread_messages, ... , users` (imports show users in the truncate set) runs immediately on `bun run seed` against whatever CONNECTION_STRING is loaded — the same var production uses.
unverified_med_low.impact: One mistyped `pnpm --filter @rivaleye/api seed` on the production VM (where .env holds the Supabase prod string, per start scripts) irreversibly wipes all users, reports, and billing-adjacent data.
unverified_med_low.fix: Refuse to run when NODE_ENV=production or when the connection string matches the prod host unless an explicit `--force-i-know` flag/env is passed; print the target host and require confirmation.

unverified_med_low.title: Swagger UI and full API spec publicly exposed in production by default
unverified_med_low.evidence: swagger.ts:6 `const enabled = process.env.SWAGGER_ENABLED !== "false"` — opt-out, not opt-in; served unauthenticated at /v1/docs (server.ts:85 mounts it before controllers/auth).
unverified_med_low.impact: Anyone can enumerate every route, parameter shape, and tag of the private API in production unless ops remembers to set SWAGGER_ENABLED=false — free reconnaissance for the retry/enqueue abuse paths above.
unverified_med_low.fix: Default to disabled when NODE_ENV=production (`enabled = SWAGGER_ENABLED === "true" || NODE_ENV !== "production"`).

unverified_med_low.title: Unauthenticated /logo/:domain proxy has no rate limit or negative-result cache
unverified_med_low.evidence: logo/index.ts:25-53 — public endpoint that, per request, serially fetches up to 3 upstream providers with 4s timeouts each (`AbortSignal.timeout(4000)`), no caching layer on the server, no per-IP throttle. Domain validation (lines 15-23) does block IPs/localhost, so SSRF is handled.
unverified_med_low.impact: An anonymous client hammering unknown domains ties up to ~12s of outbound fetch time per request on the API process and burns logo.dev quota (token-metered, line 5) — a cheap resource-exhaustion and third-party-cost vector.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add an in-process LRU cache (including negative caching of 404s), reduce to one upstream attempt for cache misses under load, and rate-limit per IP at the proxy.

unverified_med_low.title: Schema drift: migration 0013 columns/enum value exist in the database but not in the Drizzle schema or snapshots
unverified_med_low.evidence: 0013 (in _journal.json, so applied by db:migrate) runs `ALTER TYPE report_platform_job_status ADD VALUE 'retry_pending'`, adds columns next_retry_at, bg_attempts, bg_max_attempts, and creates report_platform_jobs_retry_pending_idx. The current schema (packages/api/src/db/schema/pipeline.ts:31-37, 39-69) has none of these, no TypeScript code references them (grep across packages returns nothing), and the latest snapshot (drizzle/meta/0020_snapshot.json) also omits them — verified: rpj columns list has no next_retry_at and the enum is ['queued','running','completed','failed','cancelled'].
unverified_med_low.impact: The live database permanently diverges from what drizzle-kit believes exists, and because the snapshots also lack the columns, `pnpm db:generate` will never reconcile them: dead columns, a dead index, and a dead enum value live in prod forever. Worse, any future hand or generated migration that re-introduces one of these names (e.g. re-adding that index without IF NOT EXISTS) fails mid-deploy, and any tooling that trusts the schema files (worker imports them directly) is reasoning about a table shape that isn't real.
unverified_med_low.fix: Write one custom migration dropping next_retry_at, bg_attempts, bg_max_attempts and report_platform_jobs_retry_pending_idx (the enum value can stay; PG can't drop enum values easily), then verify `drizzle-kit generate` produces an empty diff against prod.

unverified_med_low.title: Orphan migration file 0019_add_selected_platforms.sql is not in the journal and duplicates prefix 0019
unverified_med_low.evidence: `ALTER TABLE "reports" ADD COLUMN "selected_platforms" text[] DEFAULT '{}';` — this file is absent from drizzle/meta/_journal.json (entry 19 is 0019_eager_roulette), so `pnpm db:migrate` never applies it; there is no selected_platforms column in schema/reports.ts nor in meta/0020_snapshot.json, yet the file shares the 0019 index with a journaled migration.
unverified_med_low.impact: Either the column was applied to prod by hand (raw ALTER TABLE — violating the repo's own migration rule and creating the same drift class as the 0013 finding) or the file is dead weight that will mislead the next engineer into believing the column exists. If someone later adds selected_platforms to the schema, the generated ADD COLUMN migration fails on any environment where this file was run manually.
unverified_med_low.fix: Check prod (`\d reports`): if the column exists, fold it into the Drizzle schema and regenerate so snapshots match; if not, delete the file. Never keep .sql files in drizzle/ that aren't journal entries.

unverified_med_low.title: credit_transactions has no index on user_id and no unique/index on razorpay_order_id
unverified_med_low.evidence: The only index is the partial unique on razorpay_payment_id (billing.ts:38-41). getTransactions filters by user_id ordered by created_at (billing.service.ts:38-51); verifyPayment selects by razorpay_order_id (:162-166); grantCreditsForOrder — the money path hit by both the browser and the Razorpay webhook — runs `UPDATE ... WHERE razorpay_order_id = X AND razorpay_payment_id IS NULL` (:112-121) with no index and no uniqueness on razorpay_order_id, and nothing prevents two purchase rows being inserted for one order (createOrder insert at :79 has no conflict target).
unverified_med_low.impact: The webhook/verify grant seq-scans a monotonically growing money table on every payment. If duplicate rows for one order ever exist (client retry of createOrder response handling, replayed insert), the un-LIMITed UPDATE stamps the same payment_id on all of them and the partial unique index aborts the whole transaction — the payment is captured but credits are never granted, silently (webhook returns ok:true after the throw propagates as 500 and Razorpay retries into the same failure).
unverified_med_low.fix: Add `uniqueIndex on (razorpay_order_id) where razorpay_order_id is not null` and `index on (user_id, created_at)` to credit_transactions via migration.

unverified_med_low.title: healOrphanedReports GROUP-BY scans the entire ever-growing report_platform_jobs table every 30 seconds
unverified_med_low.evidence: `SELECT rpj.report_id FROM report_platform_jobs rpj GROUP BY rpj.report_id HAVING COUNT(*) = COUNT(CASE WHEN rpj.status IN ('completed','failed') ...) AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM synthesis_jobs sj WHERE sj.report_id = rpj.report_id)` — no WHERE clause, so it aggregates every job row ever created (jobs are never deleted; one row per platform x report forever). It runs inside recoverStaleJobs every 30s (recovery.ts:32-42) in the workers' polling loops.
unverified_med_low.impact: Cost grows linearly with lifetime report count and is paid every 30s on the same 5-connection pool the workers use for claiming; at tens of thousands of reports this becomes a constant multi-hundred-ms full scan + hash aggregate that competes with claim/complete transactions through PgBouncer, adding latency to the queue exactly when load is highest.
unverified_med_low.fix: Bound the scan by recency: add `WHERE rpj.created_at > now() - interval '2 days'` (orphaned-report healing only matters for recent scans), or maintain a `reports.stage = 'scraping'` filter by joining reports and only grouping jobs for non-terminal reports (reports.stage has no index either — add one if used).

unverified_med_low.title: No retention for unbounded append-only tables: report_logs, pipeline_events, mentions.raw, report_pdf_jobs.pdf_base64
unverified_med_low.evidence: grep across api and worker sources finds zero DELETE against report_logs, pipeline_events, mentions, or report_pdf_jobs.
