Every pipeline step writes report_logs (worker log()) and pipeline_events rows; mentions stores the full raw platform payload per post as NOT NULL jsonb (mentions.ts:29 `raw: jsonb("raw")...notNull()`), and copyPlatformDataFromPreviousScan re-duplicates all mentions rows (raw included) into every rescan report (reports.service.ts:188-202); completed report_pdf_jobs keep multi-MB base64 PDFs as row data forever (pipeline.ts:153, pdf-worker.ts:63).
unverified_med_low.impact: Supabase disk and backup size grow without bound and without any operational lever; large pdf_base64/raw values TOAST and slow seq scans that the missing-index findings already force; smart-rescan duplication means a popular competitor's raw corpus is stored once per rescan, multiplying storage cost per user action.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add a scheduled sweeper (worker cron loop): purge report_logs/pipeline_events older than ~30 days, null out pdf_base64 (or delete pdf jobs) after ~7 days, and either drop mentions.raw after synthesis completes or stop copying raw on rescan (copy only the columns the evidence views read).

unverified_med_low.title: reports.owner_id is nullable — orphanable reports invisible to every owner-scoped query
unverified_med_low.evidence: `owner_id: uuid("owner_id").references(() => users.id, { onDelete: "cascade" })` — no .notNull(), unlike every other owner-scoped table (competitors.ts:40, outreach.ts:16, planned-actions.ts:7, pipeline.ts:147 all use .notNull()). All read paths filter `eq(reports.owner_id, ...)` (reports.service.ts:67, dashboard.service.ts:99).
unverified_med_low.impact: Any insert path that omits owner_id (a bug, a script, worker/run-scan.ts style tooling) silently creates a report no user can see or cancel, whose jobs still consume scraper/LLM spend, and which is unreachable for cleanup through the API. NULL rows also escape the per-owner rate limit count.
unverified_med_low.fix: Backfill/delete any NULL rows, then add .notNull() and generate the migration.

unverified_med_low.title: report_complaints.external_id has no uniqueness, but report_threads and report_opportunities anchor to it as loose text
unverified_med_low.evidence: report_complaints.external_id (reports.ts:113) has no unique(report_id, external_id); report_threads.complaint_external_id (:259) and report_opportunities.anchor_complaint_external_id (:250) reference it by string with no FK. Values come straight from LLM output via the persist step.
unverified_med_low.impact: If the LLM emits two complaints with the same id (or a thread anchored to a nonexistent id), the report UI's complaint->threads/opportunity joins silently fan out to the wrong cluster or dangle — corrupt-looking reports with no error anywhere.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add unique(report_id, external_id) on report_complaints, and have persist validate anchors against the inserted complaint set (dropping or re-pointing dangling ones) before insert.

unverified_med_low.title: report_platform_stage enum is a grab-bag of two generations of stage vocabularies
unverified_med_low.evidence: report_platform_stage contains both the old vocabulary ('scrape','stage_a','stage_b','done','failed') and the new one ('fetching','storing_mentions','extracting','summarizing','completed') — including two synonyms for terminal success ('done' vs 'completed').
unverified_med_low.impact: Any consumer that checks stage equality (UI progress rendering, ops queries) must know both vocabularies; a check for stage = 'completed' misses rows finished via the 'done' path (createReport writes stage: 'done' for copied platforms, reports.service.ts:312) and vice versa — subtle wrong progress states rather than crashes.
unverified_med_low.fix: Pick one vocabulary, migrate existing rows (UPDATE ... SET stage='done' WHERE stage='completed' or vice versa), and stop writing the deprecated values; enum values can't be dropped but the schema comment should mark them dead.

unverified_med_low.title: better-auth tables missing FK indexes and expiry cleanup (accounts.user_id, sessions.user_id, verifications)
unverified_med_low.evidence: accounts (users.ts:27-43), sessions (:14-25) and verifications (:45-52) define no indexes beyond PKs and sessions.token unique; accounts.user_id and sessions.user_id are unindexed FKs, verifications.identifier is unindexed and expired rows are never deleted anywhere in the repo.
unverified_med_low.impact: better-auth looks up accounts by user_id on every credential sign-in and verifications by identifier on every email flow — seq scans that grow with user count; deleting a user cascade-scans sessions/accounts; verifications grows forever with expired magic-link/OTP rows.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add indexes on accounts(user_id), sessions(user_id), verifications(identifier), and a periodic delete of expired sessions/verifications rows.

unverified_med_low.title: planned_actions has no index for its access path and no updated_at
unverified_med_low.evidence: Table defined with no index block; listed by `eq(planned_actions.owner_id, owner_id)` ordered by created_at (planned-actions.service.ts:33-34). It is also the only table using timestamptz (`withTimezone: true`, planned-actions.ts:17) while every other table uses timestamp-without-timezone with defaultNow().
unverified_med_low.impact: Seq scan per list call as the table grows; the timezone inconsistency means cross-table timestamp comparisons (or a future non-UTC server) silently skew — the queue recovery logic already compares app-generated Date objects against DB now() on naive timestamps (recovery.ts:58 vs claim.ts locked_at now()), which only works while the DB runs UTC.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add index on (owner_id, created_at); standardize on withTimezone: true for new columns and document that the DB must remain UTC until existing columns are migrated.

unverified_med_low.title: All migrations create indexes non-CONCURRENTLY — future index additions will lock hot tables
unverified_med_low.evidence: Every CREATE INDEX across drizzle/*.sql (0000, 0001, 0002, 0003, 0005, 0006, 0013, 0016, 0017, 0020) is plain `CREATE INDEX` — no CONCURRENTLY anywhere (grep confirms). deploy.sh runs db:migrate in-line with deploys.
unverified_med_low.impact: Harmless today, but the fixes this audit requires (indexes on reports and the 15 report_* child tables, mentions retention, etc.) will be applied to already-populated tables; a plain CREATE INDEX takes SHARE lock and blocks all writes — on mentions/report_logs at production size this stalls every running scan for the duration of the build, during a deploy.
unverified_med_low.fix: For indexes on populated tables, use hand-written migrations with `CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY` executed outside a transaction (drizzle supports `--> statement-breakpoint` with transactional off via custom migration), or apply them via a maintenance script before the schema migration lands.

unverified_med_low.title: Sonar discovery runs redundantly once per platform job — up to 9 duplicate paid Perplexity calls per report
unverified_med_low.evidence: ensureDiscovery() is called from every source job (source-worker.ts:160-162) and only checks `reports.discovered_ids` before making its own `discoverCompetitorIdentifiers()` call; the doc comment admits 'Multiple concurrent source jobs may call this; we tolerate a small amount of redundant Sonar work'. With 9 enabled platforms fanning out simultaneously and MAX_CONCURRENT_SOURCE=8, up to 8 jobs pass the NULL check before any writes.
unverified_med_low.impact: At thousands of users, every report multiplies the web-grounded Perplexity Sonar spend by up to ~8× and adds redundant 60s LLM calls to each platform job's critical path. Concurrent conflicting results are handled (set-if-NULL), so this is purely cost/latency waste, but it scales linearly with report volume.
unverified_med_low.fix: Single-flight discovery per report: either run discovery once at enqueue time in the API service before inserting platform jobs, or use a pg advisory lock / `UPDATE ... WHERE discovered_ids IS NULL RETURNING` claim so only one job performs the Sonar call while peers poll the column.

unverified_med_low.title: Website scraper launches a full Chromium per job inside the worker process — up to 8 concurrent browsers on the single shared GCE VM
unverified_med_low.evidence: `const browser = await chromium.launch({ headless: true });` runs per crawlWebsite() invocation, then crawls up to PAGE_LIMIT=15 pages serially at 30s timeout each (~up to 8 min/job). No pooling, no cap on concurrent launches beyond the generic MAX_CONCURRENT_SOURCE=8, no robots.txt check.
unverified_med_low.impact: Each Chromium instance costs ~300-500MB RSS plus CPU; a spike where 8 website jobs run concurrently can consume 2.5-4GB on the one VM that also hosts the API, synth worker (which itself runs Puppeteer for PDFs), and web processes — OOM-killing PM2 processes and taking down the whole product. Also, crawling arbitrary competitor sites while ignoring robots.txt from the product's own IP is a legal/blocking exposure.
unverified_med_low.fix: Route website crawls through the existing Browserless account (consistent with linkedin/twitter) or maintain a single shared browser instance with a page-pool and a dedicated semaphore (e.g. max 2 concurrent website jobs). Honor robots.txt / add crawl-delay.

unverified_med_low.title: Dev.to scraper swallows all fetch errors into empty arrays — provider outage yields a silent 0-post 'completed' platform
unverified_med_low.evidence: searchArticles ends with `.catch(() => []);` (client.ts:72), and devto/index.ts:24-25 wraps both tag fetches in `.catch(() => [])`. So a dev.to 5xx/outage/429 on the primary search path produces an empty result instead of a thrown ScraperError; source-worker then marks the job completed with posts_count 0 (source-worker.ts:192-217).
unverified_med_low.impact: During any dev.to incident (or if they block the worker IP), every scan quietly completes with zero devto data — no retry, no failed status, no alert; the report is silently thinner. Violates the package's own rule 4 ('Never silently return [] on error'). Same pattern, lower stakes, in producthunt fetchComments (producthunt/client.ts:99 `catch { return []; }`).
unverified_med_low.fix: Remove the blanket catches on the primary data path; let apiGet's ScraperError propagate so the job retries and eventually fails visibly. Keep catch-to-empty only for genuinely optional enrichment (per-article comments).

unverified_med_low.title: App Store review pagination fails the whole platform job on a single non-404 error page, discarding all fetched data across all 5 apps
unverified_med_low.evidence: `if (!res.ok) throw new ScraperError("appstore", `reviews HTTP ${res.status} (page ${page})`);` inside the page loop, called from `Promise.all(apps.map(...))` in appstore/index.ts:44-49 — one 503/429 on page 4 of app 3 rejects the entire Promise.all and throws away the hundreds of reviews already fetched.
unverified_med_low.impact: Apple's customerreviews RSS endpoint is notoriously flaky (intermittent 503s and has been progressively deprecated). One bad page → whole appstore job fails → full retry re-fetches all 25 pages from scratch (3×), and after max_attempts the platform is marked failed even though 90% of the data was in hand. Degrades a common platform to all-or-nothing.
unverified_med_low.fix: On a non-404 error page: retry that page once with a short backoff, then break the pagination loop keeping accumulated reviews (log a partial-result warning) instead of throwing. Only throw if page 1 of every app fails (true outage).

unverified_med_low.title: Provider tokens embedded in URL query strings and interpolated into error messages — secrets leak into logs and the last_error DB column
unverified_med_low.evidence: Apify: `...run-sync-get-dataset-items?token=${token}...` then on failure `throw new Error(`Apify request failed for actor ${actorId}: ${String(err)}`)` (client.ts:21) — Bun/undici fetch errors frequently include the request URL, i.e. the token. Browserless: `fetch(`${BROWSERLESS_BASE}/function?token=${this.token}`)` (linkedin/index.ts:102, twitter/index.ts:158) — same exposure via error causes; ScraperError causes are logged by source-worker and error messages are persisted to report_platform_jobs.last_error.
unverified_med_low.impact: Paid-provider API tokens end up in pino stdout logs (shipped wherever logs go), PM2 log files on the VM, and the Postgres last_error column readable via the API/dashboard — anyone with log or DB read access can exfiltrate the Apify/Browserless tokens and run up spend on those accounts.
unverified_med_low.fix: Pass tokens via headers (Apify: `Authorization: Bearer`; Browserless supports header auth) instead of query params; scrub/redact token patterns in ScraperError messages before logging/persisting.

unverified_med_low.title: Twitter scrape workload (~17 page navigations) does not fit its 60s Browserless budget — chronic timeouts convert into 3 paid retries per scan
unverified_med_low.evidence: The function script performs: people search (2.5s wait) + profile load (2s) + scrape of 10 profile posts, then navigates into EACH post for replies (10 × [goto 15s-timeout + 1.5s wait + 2 scroll×0.8s]), then mention search + up to 5 more tweet-detail navigations — comment at line 157 says '60s max on this plan' and the request pins `&timeout=60000`. Just the fixed sleeps sum to ~45s before any page-load time.
unverified_med_low.impact: On any competitor with an active profile, the 60s server-side timeout fires mid-run; Browserless returns an error, the scraper throws ScraperError, and the job retries up to max_attempts=3 — i.e. 3 paid Browserless sessions per scan that each burn ~60s of unit time and likely all fail, then the platform is marked failed. Predictable cost with near-zero yield at scale.
unverified_med_low.fix: Track an elapsed-time budget inside the script and return whatever was collected before ~50s (partial results are valid — allPosts is accumulated incrementally); cut reply navigation to the top 2-3 posts, or upgrade the plan timeout to match the workload.

unverified_med_low.title: Reddit env overrides parsed with unguarded parseInt — a malformed value silently disables the scraper (0 search terms, 0 posts, job 'completed')
unverified_med_low.evidence: `const MAX_SEARCH_TERMS = process.env["REDDIT_MAX_TERMS"] ? parseInt(process.env["REDDIT_MAX_TERMS"], 10) : 5;` — `REDDIT_MAX_TERMS=five` gives NaN, then `SEARCH_TEMPLATES.slice(0, NaN)` returns [] and the fetch loop never executes; MAX_TOTAL_POSTS also becomes NaN so the early-exit comparison is always false.
unverified_med_low.impact: A typo'd env var on the VM makes every Reddit scrape return zero posts while jobs report 'completed' — the highest-value platform silently vanishes from all reports with nothing in the logs but 'termCount: 0'. (Contrast pg-runner's clampInt which guards NaN.)
unverified_med_low.fix: Reuse the clampInt pattern (NaN → default, clamp to sane bounds) for REDDIT_MAX_TERMS and REDDIT_MAX_POSTS_PER_TERM.

unverified_med_low.title: getScraper called with unvalidated platform string from the DB — unknown platform yields undefined and an unclassified TypeError retried 3 times
unverified_med_low.evidence: `const scraper = getScraper(platform as any);` — getScraper's switch (scrapers/src/index.ts:30-59) has no default case, so an unknown platform string (e.g. a legacy 'g2' row or future rename) returns undefined and `scraper.fetch(...)` throws `TypeError: undefined is not an object`. Not a PermanentError, so it takes the full 3-attempt retry cycle before failing.
unverified_med_low.impact: Stale or renamed platform rows in report_platform_jobs waste ~8 minutes of retries per job and surface as a confusing TypeError in last_error instead of a clear 'unknown platform' message; fan-in for the report is delayed accordingly.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add a default case in getScraper throwing a descriptive error, validate job.platform against ENABLED_PLATFORMS before fetching, and classify unknown-platform as PermanentError so it fails fast.

unverified_med_low.title: LinkedIn fallback externalId is positional ('li-0', 'li-1') — non-deterministic IDs defeat the mentions dedup key across retries
unverified_med_low.evidence: `const id = el.getAttribute('data-id') ?? 'li-' + results.length;` — when LinkedIn omits data-id, the externalId is the item's scroll position, which changes between runs as the feed reorders. The mentions unique index is (report_id, platform, external_id) with onConflictDoNothing (source-worker.ts persistMentions).
unverified_med_low.impact: On a retry after partial failure, the same post can reappear at a different position and be inserted twice under a different 'li-N' id (duplicate mentions feeding Stage A), or two different posts can collide on the same 'li-N' and one is silently dropped. Low volume (only when data-id is missing) but corrupts the dedup guarantee.
unverified_med_low.fix: Derive the fallback id from stable content — e.g. a hash of the post URL (href) or of author+text — instead of the array index; skip posts with neither data-id nor href.

unverified_med_low.title: Stage A results are not persisted until Stage B succeeds — retries re-pay every Stage A LLM call
unverified_med_low.evidence: The retry cache reads report_platform_briefs (source-worker.ts:440-457), but in the pg-runner path that row is only ever written at the END of Stage B (runStageBSummarizationStep, source-worker.ts:571-591). There is no extract-only persist after Stage A (the dead Inngest path had one, worker/src/llm/stage-a.ts:111-132, but it is not in ecosystem.config.cjs). Additionally Stage A batches run via `Promise.all` (source-worker.ts:476-498): one batch rejection fails the job immediately while sibling in-flight LLM calls keep running and their tokens are discarded.
unverified_med_low.impact: Any Stage B failure (schema error, timeout, worker crash between A and B) forces the retry to re-run ALL Stage A batches — for a 125-post Reddit job that is 3 x ~20k-token calls re-paid per attempt, up to max_attempts times. Combined with the Promise.all fail-fast waste, a flaky hour at OpenRouter multiplies Stage A spend ~3x across every affected scan with zero user-visible benefit.
unverified_med_low.fix: Persist the merged Stage A extract into report_platform_briefs (with empty summary) immediately after Stage A completes — the cache check already handles this shape. Optionally use Promise.allSettled and fail only after all batches settle, retrying just the failed batches.

unverified_med_low.title: triggerResynthesis race can re-run the entire C/D/E synthesis with no new data; each late platform re-pays full synthesis
unverified_med_low.evidence: Step 10 of every successful source job calls `triggerResynthesis(job.report_id)` (source-worker.ts:263) immediately after fanInCheck (line 259) creates the synthesis job. The synth worker polls every 500ms (pg-runner/index.ts:450) and can claim the job (status -> running) before step 10's transaction runs; resynthesis.ts:45-51 then sets rerun_requested=true, and synthesis-worker.ts:204-236 deletes all checkpoints and re-queues a full C/D/E re-run after the first run finishes — a complete duplicate of the scan's most expensive LLM work for zero data change. Separately, resynthesis.ts:65 resets attempt_count to 0 on every requeue, so each late-recovered platform grants a fresh retry budget and its own full synthesis rebuild.
unverified_med_low.impact: For the last-completing platform of a normal scan, whenever the synth worker wins the 0-500ms race, synthesis runs twice: ~2x the ~400-600k synthesis prompt tokens and minutes of extra latency, on a nontrivial fraction of all scans at load. On flaky-platform scans, N late recoveries = N full synthesis rebuilds with unbounded retry budget.
unverified_med_low.fix: In processSourceJob, skip triggerResynthesis when fanInCheck just created the job in this same call (have fanInCheck return the outcome), or have triggerResynthesis compare a briefs-updated-at watermark against the synthesis job's started_at and no-op when no brief is newer than the in-flight run. Cap total resynthesis count per report.

unverified_med_low.title: LLM 429/backoff handling ignores Retry-After and there is no global concurrency limit across ~40 parallel LLM calls
unverified_med_low.evidence: openrouter.ts:158-159 `if (!res.ok) { throw new LlmHttpError(res.status, await res.text()); }` — response headers (Retry-After / X-RateLimit-Reset) are discarded; retry is fixed exponential capped at 30s with maxAttempts<=3 (openrouter.ts:61-62, 114). Concurrency is uncoordinated: scrape worker runs up to 8 source jobs (pg-runner/index.ts:55) each firing ceil(posts/50) parallel Stage A batches (source-worker.ts:476), while the synth worker runs 2 synthesis jobs each firing Stage D synth + 5 parallel role sections (stage-d-role.ts:140-146) + summary concurrently. No semaphore, queue, or adaptive throttle exists anywhere.
unverified_med_low.impact: A traffic spike (thousands of users -> many concurrent scans) pushes ~30-50 simultaneous OpenRouter requests. Once the account hits its rate limit, every call 429s, each retries at most 3 times within ~90s regardless of the provider's advertised reset time, jobs then fail and re-queue at the job level (30s/2m/5m), re-paying full prompts. The system thrashes: high spend, low throughput, scans wedging at Stage A across the fleet.
unverified_med_low.fix: Parse Retry-After/x-ratelimit headers on 429 and sleep accordingly (respecting the caller timeout); add a process-wide semaphore (e.g. max 8-12 in-flight LLM calls per process, env-tunable) that all complete() calls acquire.

unverified_med_low.title: Schema-validation failures are never retried at the client level; JSON detection is prefix-only with no repair (except Stage E)
unverified_med_low.evidence: complete() runs zod validation AFTER callWithRetry returns (openrouter.ts:99-104), so an LlmSchemaError bypasses the retry loop entirely (isTransient() at openrouter.ts:44-59 doesn't recognize it). looksLikeJson (openrouter.ts:173-176) only checks the first character — a truncated response passes and later throws LlmJsonParseError, which is also non-transient. Consequence at call sites: one malformed Stage A batch response throws out of runStageAExtract (source-worker.ts:491-496) and fails the WHOLE source job, triggering a full scrape+Stage A job retry (see Stage A cache finding). Only stage-d-role.ts (ensureSection, lines 61-111) and stage-e-refine.ts (extractJson truncation repair, lines 23-37) implement proper parse-level retry/repair; Stage A, Stage B, Stage D synth, and discover.ts get none.
unverified_med_low.impact: Non-deterministic model output (the single most common LLM failure mode, amplified by temperature 1.0) converts a 1-cent re-ask into a full job retry costing the entire platform's scrape + all Stage A batches, and after max_attempts a permanently failed platform — reports go partial/failed because of one bad JSON emission.
unverified_med_low.fix: On LlmSchemaError/LlmJsonParseError inside complete(), retry once with the RETRY_SUFFIX corrective prompt (the mechanism already exists at openrouter.ts:41-42,122) and feed zod issues back to the model; apply stage-e's truncated-JSON recovery in parseJson().

unverified_med_low.title: temperature 1.0 default and no JSON response_format for strict-schema extraction
unverified_med_low.evidence: openrouter.ts:81 `this.temperature = opts.temperature ?? 1.0;` — no call site overrides it (all construct with only apiKey+model, e.g. source-worker.ts:50-53, run.ts:60). The request body (openrouter.ts:147-155) never sets `response_format: { type: "json_object" }` even though every pipeline call demands strict JSON output.
unverified_med_low.impact: Maximum sampling temperature on JSON-extraction tasks measurably raises malformed/truncated-JSON and schema-mismatch rates, which (per the previous finding) escalate into full job retries. Higher retry rate = higher cost and more wedged/partial scans, especially on the 16k-token Stage D and 32k-token Stage E completions where truncation risk is largest.
unverified_med_low.fix: Default temperature to ~0.2-0.3 for schema-bearing requests (or expose per-request temperature) and send response_format json_object (OpenRouter forwards it to supporting providers).

unverified_med_low.title: Sonar discovery runs up to N-platforms times per report (redundant paid web-grounded calls)
unverified_med_low.evidence: ensureDiscovery (source-worker.ts:64-100) is check-then-act: read reports.discovered_ids, and if NULL run `discoverCompetitorIdentifiers` (Perplexity Sonar via OpenRouter, discover.ts:78-95, 60s timeout, 2 attempts). All ~9 platform jobs for a fresh report are claimed near-simultaneously (8 concurrent slots, 500ms poll), all observe NULL, and all pay the Sonar call. The comment at lines 60-63 admits it: "Multiple concurrent source jobs may call this; we tolerate a small amount of redundant Sonar work".
unverified_med_low.impact: Up to 8-9 identical Sonar web-search calls per scan instead of 1 — Sonar is one of the pricier per-call models (web grounding), so this is a direct ~8x multiplier on discovery cost for every single scan at launch scale, plus 9 wasted 60s slots at scan start.
unverified_med_low.fix: Single-flight it: take `pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(reportId || ':discovery'))` around the check-and-call, or have the API pre-run discovery once at scan creation before inserting platform jobs.

unverified_med_low.title: Stage E quality fallback is silent and the E checkpoint is loaded without validation
unverified_med_low.evidence: runStageERefine catches ALL errors and returns the draft (stage-e-refine.ts:65-75) with fellBackToDraft=true; run.ts:339-341 only writes a warn row to report_logs — the report is still marked completed with no flag on the reports row, no metric, no alert. And when re-loading checkpoints, run.ts:352 does `refined = checkpoints.get("E") as unknown as SynthOutput;` (same at run.ts:188) — a raw cast with no synthOutputSchema.safeParse, unlike the C and D checkpoints which are parsed (run.ts:139, 165).
unverified_med_low.impact: Observability gap: if OpenRouter degrades for a day, every report silently ships the unrefined draft and nobody notices (the only trace is buried in report_logs JSON). The unvalidated E cast means a corrupt/legacy checkpoint row flows straight into persistReport and can write malformed report data or crash persist mid-way on a retry path.
unverified_med_low.fix: Store fellBackToDraft on the report row (or a pipeline_quality column) and count it as a metric; validate the E checkpoint with synthOutputSchema.safeParse and fall back to re-running Stage E when it fails.

unverified_med_low.title: PDF worker: user session cookies stored plaintext in Postgres; fresh Chromium per job with no crash cleanup
unverified_med_low.evidence: pdf-worker.ts:57 passes `job.session_cookie` from the report_pdf_jobs row — the requester's live better-auth session cookie is persisted plaintext in the DB from enqueue until job completion/failure (only then nulled, lines 63-64, 83). render.ts:34-37 launches a brand-new `puppeteer.launch({ headless: true, args: ["--no-sandbox", ...] })` per job; browser.close() is in finally (render.ts:71-73), but a PM2 kill/max_memory_restart (ecosystem: max_memory_restart '1G' on the shared VM) mid-render orphans the Chrome process tree, and there is no startup sweep for stray chromes.
unverified_med_low.impact: Security: anyone with DB read access (or a backup/log leak) can hijack active user sessions via the queued cookie rows; failed jobs keep cookies until the retry cycle ends. Ops: on the single GCE VM, repeated worker restarts under memory pressure accumulate zombie Chromium processes (~150-300MB each), eventually starving the scrape/synth workers on the same box.
unverified_med_low.fix: Replace the forwarded session cookie with a short-lived single-purpose signed token the export page accepts (or encrypt the cookie at rest with a worker-held key and expire rows aggressively). Reuse one browser instance across jobs with a page-per-job model, and on worker boot kill leftover chrome processes / use puppeteer's pipe+userDataDir cleanup.

unverified_med_low.title: No provider abstraction or env-injectable mock — OpenRouter base URL/model hardwired at every call site
unverified_med_low.evidence: OpenRouterClient supports constructor injection (`fetcher`, `baseUrl`, openrouter.ts:27-28, 82-83) but no env reads: `this.baseUrl = opts.baseUrl ?? DEFAULT_BASE;`. Every production call site constructs `new OpenRouterClient({ apiKey: readOpenRouterApiKey(), model: LLM_MODEL })` with a module-level singleton (source-worker.ts:47-55, run.ts:56-62, reports.service.ts:36-43, discover.ts:29-38) — no OPENROUTER_BASE_URL, no LLM_PROVIDER switch, and one global model for every stage.
unverified_med_low.impact: You cannot point staging/e2e at a mock LLM server or a cheaper per-stage model without code changes and redeploy; load-testing the queue at launch therefore burns real OpenRouter spend, and an OpenRouter-wide outage has no fallback provider path despite ANTHROPIC_API_KEY/OPENAI_API_KEY existing in .env.example.
unverified_med_low.fix: Read `process.env.OPENROUTER_BASE_URL` into DEFAULT_BASE fallback and add optional per-stage model env vars (e.g. OPENROUTER_MODEL_SYNTH). A tiny LlmProvider interface with an OpenRouter impl would also unlock a mock provider and a secondary-provider failover.

unverified_med_low.title: Dead Inngest LLM worker retains unbatched, untimeouted Stage A path
unverified_med_low.evidence: stage-a.ts:87-103 calls `runStageAExtract({ llm: getLlm(), ctx, platform, posts: posts.map(...) })` with NO LlmCallOptions — no timeout, default 3 attempts — and passes ALL of a platform's mentions in a single LLM call (no 50-post batching, unlike source-worker.ts:467-471). This entry point (worker/src/llm/index.ts) is not in ecosystem.config.cjs (only api/landing/web/scrape/synth run), so it is dead in production, but it still compiles, still reads env, and INNGEST_FAILURE_TRACE.md / config.ts keep the engine switch alive.
unverified_med_low.impact: If anyone flips REPORT_PIPELINE_ENGINE=inngest or starts worker-llm during an incident, Stage A sends unbounded prompts (125 Reddit posts x 1500 chars in one call) with no timeout — hung calls hold the process and token blowups return. Dead-but-runnable duplicate pipelines are a foot-gun during on-call.
unverified_med_low.fix: Delete the Inngest path (src/llm/, src/inngest/, the engine switch) or at minimum make it throw at startup in production; the pg-runner is the only deployed engine.

unverified_med_low.title: Migrations applied while old API/worker code still serves; no migration rollback if reload fails
unverified_med_low.evidence: deploy.sh order: build (line 25) → `pnpm db:migrate` (line 35) → `pm2 startOrReload` (line 40). Between lines 35 and 40 the old in-memory API and both workers run against the migrated schema. If startOrReload fails, the migration is already committed with no down-migration mechanism (drizzle-kit migrate is forward-only here).
unverified_med_low.impact: Any destructive or renaming migration (column drop/rename, NOT NULL addition) breaks the still-running old code for the reload window — and permanently if the reload fails, since there is no rollback: old code + new schema until manual intervention. Workers mid-scrape write to the old shapes and fail or corrupt rows.
unverified_med_low.fix: Enforce expand/contract (backwards-compatible) migrations as a hard rule; run migrate immediately before reload with a health check after; document that destructive migrations require a two-deploy sequence.

unverified_med_low.title: Swagger/Scalar API docs exposed in production by default (opt-out, not opt-in)
unverified_med_low.evidence: `const enabled = process.env.SWAGGER_ENABLED !== "false";` — enabled unless explicitly disabled; served at `/v1/docs`. SWAGGER_ENABLED appears in no .env.example (root, packages/api, packages/worker), so it is almost certainly unset on the VM. docs/deployment-plan.md line 576 itself lists "API Swagger UI disabled in production" as an unresolved checklist item.
unverified_med_low.impact: The complete internal API surface (auth routes, billing/Razorpay webhook paths, report endpoints, schemas) is publicly enumerable at https://<api>/v1/docs, materially easing endpoint probing and abuse of unauthenticated or weakly-limited routes.
unverified_med_low.fix: Flip to opt-in: `const enabled = process.env.SWAGGER_ENABLED === "true"`, or gate on NODE_ENV !== 'production'. Add SWAGGER_ENABLED to .env.example.

unverified_med_low.title: Frontends served via unpinned `npx -y serve` / `npx -y http-server` resolved from npm at every process start
unverified_med_low.evidence: Line 33: `npx -y http-server packages/landing/dist -p 3000 -c-1`; line 44: `npx -y serve -s packages/web/dist -l 4004`. Neither package is in any package.json; `-y` auto-installs the latest version from the registry on cache miss.
unverified_med_low.impact: A PM2 restart during an npm registry outage or VM egress problem leaves the landing page/app down (crash-loop every 4s). Worse, `npx -y` with no version pin executes whatever the registry serves as latest — a compromised `serve`/`http-server` release runs on the production VM with access to the repo directory containing .env.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add pinned `serve`/`http-server` as devDependencies (or use a static file server built into the API/nginx), and reference the workspace binary so nothing is fetched at process start.

unverified_med_low.title: Deploy is not pinned to the triggering commit and has no concurrency lock
unverified_med_low.evidence: The SSH command runs `git pull origin main && bash deploy.sh` — it deploys whatever main's HEAD is at execution time, not $COMMIT_SHA. Nothing (no flock, no Cloud Build queueing config) prevents two builds from running deploy.sh concurrently on the VM.
unverified_med_low.impact: Two pushes in quick succession trigger two builds that interleave `pnpm install`, turbo builds, `db:migrate`, and `pm2 startOrReload` in the same directory — corrupting node_modules/dist mid-build and potentially double-applying reloads; the earlier build can also silently deploy the later commit unreviewed by its own gate run.
unverified_med_low.fix: Checkout `$COMMIT_SHA` explicitly (`git fetch && git checkout $COMMIT_SHA`) and wrap deploy.sh in `flock /tmp/rivaleye-deploy.lock`; or restrict the Cloud Build trigger to serialized builds.

unverified_med_low.title: No error alerting or uptime monitoring anywhere — /health exists but nothing consumes it
unverified_med_low.evidence: The /health endpoint does real work (DB ping, queue-stall detection with 15-min threshold, server.ts:16,89-121), but grep for sentry/datadog/logtail/uptime across packages/api and packages/worker package.json + src finds nothing; the repo has no .github/ directory, no monitoring config, and docs/deployment-plan.md line 566 lists "Error alerting" as unresolved. PM2 does not perform HTTP health checks.
unverified_med_low.impact: A dead worker (queue: "stalled"), DB outage (503), or crash-looping API is detected by no system. Given the good stall-detection logic already built, an outage still surfaces only when a user complains — silent failure of the whole scan pipeline for hours.
unverified_med_low.fix: Point an external uptime checker (GCP Uptime Checks are free-tier, or UptimeRobot) at /health and alert when status != 200 or queue == "stalled"; add Sentry (bun-compatible) to api and worker for unhandled errors.

unverified_med_low.title: Production install is not lockfile-frozen
unverified_med_low.evidence: `pnpm install` (line 16) without `--frozen-lockfile`, run directly on the production VM. docs/deployment-plan.md and the abandoned Dockerfile plan both specify `--frozen-lockfile`.
unverified_med_low.impact: If a package.json/lockfile mismatch lands, prod silently resolves fresh (possibly newer, semver-range) dependency versions that were never tested locally, and mutates pnpm-lock.yaml on the VM — causing drift and non-reproducible deploys under `git reset --hard`.
unverified_med_low.fix: Use `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` in deploy.sh.

unverified_med_low.title: Builds and type-checks run on the production VM, starving live API/workers during every deploy
unverified_med_low.evidence: deploy.sh runs the full workspace type-check and build on the serving VM; its own comments admit resource starvation: line 13-14 "Cap Node heap so vite/astro don't get OOM-killed on a small VM", line 23-24 "Running vite + astro check + bun build in parallel starves a small VM and the build hangs". cloudbuild.yaml timeout is 7200s.
unverified_med_low.impact: For up to the full build duration, CPU/memory pressure from tsc+vite+astro competes with the live API (auth latency spikes) and both workers (scrape/LLM throughput drops, poll loops and DB queries slow, risking false stale-job reclaims and OOM kills of the 1500M synth process). Every deploy degrades production for all users.
unverified_med_low.fix: Move type-check/build to Cloud Build (it is already in the loop) and ship artifacts to the VM; VM steps should be only: fetch artifacts, migrate, reload.

unverified_med_low.title: PM2 'zero-downtime reload' is actually kill+restart (fork mode via bash wrapper), and config changes silently don't apply
unverified_med_low.evidence: Every app uses `script: 'bash'` with `args: -lc '...'` (lines 20-21 etc.), which forces PM2 fork mode — `startOrReload` cannot do cluster-style zero-downtime reload and instead kills then restarts, contradicting deploy.sh line 37's "zero-downtime reload" comment. The file's own NOTE (lines 12-14) admits `pm2 does not apply script/args changes on startOrReload` and requires a manual `pm2 delete all && pm2 start`.
unverified_med_low.impact: Every deploy drops in-flight API requests (hard kill of the bun server plus 4s restart_delay = multi-second API downtime per deploy). Separately, any edit to ecosystem.config.cjs commands ships through the pipeline but silently never takes effect until someone remembers the manual delete/start ritual — production runs stale process definitions with no signal.
unverified_med_low.fix: Run bun directly (`script: 'src/server.ts'`, `interpreter: '~/.bun/bin/bun'`) so PM2 manages the real process; for true zero-downtime either run 2 API instances behind a local nginx or accept and health-gate the restart. Add a deploy-time diff check that forces delete+start when ecosystem.config.cjs changed.

unverified_med_low.title: No CI on pull requests — the only quality gate runs on the production VM at deploy time
unverified_med_low.evidence: The repo has no .github/ directory (verified by ls). The only automated checks anywhere are deploy.sh's type-check/build, executed on the prod VM after main has already been updated. `pnpm lint` and the worker's vitest/bun test suites (packages/worker/package.json test scripts) are never run by any pipeline.
unverified_med_low.impact: Broken code merges to main freely; the first time it is ever type-checked is mid-deploy on the production box (see the stale-working-tree finding), and tests/lint are never run at all — regressions in queue logic (the tested area, POSTGRES_RUNNER_TESTS.md) ship unverified.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add a GitHub Actions workflow running `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile && pnpm type-check && pnpm lint && pnpm --filter @rivaleye/worker test` on PRs and pushes to main, and make the Cloud Build trigger require it.

unverified_med_low.title: No verified backup/PITR story for the single Postgres holding data, queue, and auth
unverified_med_low.evidence: Supabase Postgres is simultaneously the app DB, the job queue, and the better-auth store (deployment-plan.md line 38: "Postgres IS the queue"). The pre-launch checklist item "Supabase Point-in-Time Recovery enabled... before any user data is written" (line 567) is unchecked, and no backup automation, restore runbook, or pg_dump cron exists anywhere in the repo.
unverified_med_low.impact: A bad migration, the seed script (which truncates core tables per CLAUDE.md), or operator error is unrecoverable beyond whatever the current Supabase plan's default daily snapshot covers — potentially 24h of user data, payments/credit state (Razorpay webhooks grant credits), and reports lost.
unverified_med_low.fix: Enable Supabase PITR before launch, verify a restore once, and document the restore runbook; optionally add a nightly pg_dump to GCS as a second copy.

unverified_med_low.title: deploy.sh exports every secret into the deploy shell and PM2 daemon state
unverified_med_low.evidence: Lines 29-31: `set -a; source ./.env; set +a` exports all secrets (DB connection string, Razorpay secrets, LLM keys, Apify token) as environment variables for the remainder of the script; `pm2 startOrReload ... --update-env` (line 40) then snapshots that environment into the PM2 daemon, and `pm2 save` persists process env into ~/.pm2/dump.pm2.
unverified_med_low.impact: Secrets propagate to every child process of the deploy (turbo, all build scripts and their transitive npm deps — including the unpinned npx-installed servers on later restarts) and are persisted in the PM2 dump file; any compromised build-time dependency can read production credentials it has no need for.
unverified_med_low.fix: Source .env only for the migrate step in a subshell (`( set -a; source ./.env; set +a; pnpm db:migrate )`), and let runtime processes keep loading it themselves via `bun --env-file` instead of --update-env inheritance.

unverified_med_low.title: Deploy pipeline depends on a personal user account and home directory
unverified_med_low.evidence: `gcloud compute ssh faizan514pathan@rivaleye-server ... 'cd /home/faizan514pathan/rivaleye-v3 ...'` — the production checkout, PM2 daemon, and logs live under an individual's home directory and SSH identity.
unverified_med_low.impact: Offboarding or disabling that individual's account breaks all deploys and orphans the PM2 daemon (PM2 daemons are per-user); file permissions tie production state to one person's account.
unverified_med_low.fix: Create a dedicated service user (e.g. `rivaleye`) owning /opt/rivaleye and its PM2 daemon; have Cloud Build SSH as that user via a dedicated service account.

unverified_med_low.title: ReportPage error branch is unreachable — failed report fetch shows an infinite skeleton
unverified_med_low.evidence: report.tsx:52-58: `if (query.isLoading || !query.data) { return <ReportSkeleton/> }` runs BEFORE the `query.isError` check at line 60. On error (retry: 0, query-client.ts:14), isLoading is false but data is undefined, so `!query.data` is true and the skeleton renders forever; the 'Could not load report' Alert at report.tsx:60-71 can never render (error + cached data would skip both).
unverified_med_low.impact: Any /reports/:id fetch failure — deleted report, 403/404 from another user's id, 5xx during an incident, expired session — renders a permanent loading skeleton with no error message and no retry. Users perceive the scan as wedged; support cannot distinguish 'slow' from 'failed'.
unverified_med_low.fix: Check `query.isError` first, then `if (query.isLoading || !query.data)`; render the Alert with a retry button on error.

unverified_med_low.title: Open redirect via unsanitized returnTo on the sign-in page
unverified_med_low.evidence: signin.tsx:55 `const returnTo = searchParams.get("returnTo") ?? CONFIG.auth.redirectPath;` then line 88 `navigate(returnTo);` after successful email sign-in, and line 101 `callbackURL: `${window.location.origin}${returnTo}`` for OAuth. No validation. Contrast GuestGuard (auth/guard/guest-guard.tsx:18-20) which explicitly allows only paths starting with "/" and not "//" — the same sanitization is missing where the redirect actually happens after login. react-router-dom ^6.28 (package.json:39) data routers perform a document navigation for absolute/external URLs passed to navigate().
unverified_med_low.impact: A phishing link like https://app.rivaleye.com/signin?returnTo=https://evil.example redirects the victim to an attacker page immediately after they type their real credentials — classic post-login open redirect used to chain credential-reprompt phishing. The OAuth callbackURL concatenation also mis-builds URLs for hostile input.
unverified_med_low.fix: Reuse the GuestGuard sanitizer at the point of navigation: accept only returnTo values that start with "/" and not "//" (and contain no scheme), else fall back to CONFIG.auth.redirectPath.

unverified_med_low.title: Scraped/LLM-derived URLs rendered as clickable hrefs without protocol allowlisting (javascript: XSS vector)
unverified_med_low.evidence: evidence-drawer.tsx:174-182 renders `Source` where source_url flows from scraped pipeline data via normalizeEvidenceSection (scan-report.tsx:92 `source_url: (obj.source_url as string | null) ?? null` — no validation, explicit comment at scan-report.tsx:320-322 says the web layer intentionally does not enforce the contract). Same pattern: thread-modal.tsx:104 `href={data.url}`, outreach-drawer.tsx:109, source-evidence-section.tsx:52, growth.tsx:1022/1204/1452. No sanitizer/allowlist anywhere (grep for DOMPurify/sanitize returned nothing).
unverified_med_low.impact: Scraped posts are hostile input and URLs pass through an LLM synthesis stage (prompt-injectable). A `javascript:` or `data:` URL surviving the pipeline becomes a one-click XSS in an authenticated session — executing in the app origin it can read the localStorage query cache (all report data) and issue cookie-authenticated API calls. React escapes text bodies, so hrefs are the remaining injection surface.
unverified_med_low.fix: Centralize a safeUrl() helper that parses the URL and only returns it when protocol is http:/https: (else null/hide the link); apply it to every external href sourced from pipeline data.

unverified_med_low.title: Retry-failed-platforms invalidates the wrong query key — UI never reflects the retry
unverified_med_low.evidence: report.tsx:120-125 `onRetryFailed` calls `queryClient.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: ["report", report.id] })`, but the report detail query key is `reportsKeys.detail(id)` = ["reports", "detail", id] (use-reports.ts:59-65). Same class of bug in report-in-progress.tsx:249-251 which invalidates ["report-progress", report.id] while the progress query key is reportsKeys.section(id, "progress") = ["reports", "detail", id, "progress"] (use-reports.ts:123).
unverified_med_low.impact: On a completed/partial report (status terminal, so refetchInterval is off per use-reports.ts:103-107), clicking 'retry failed platforms' fires the API calls but the invalidation is a no-op: status, partial flag, and failed_platforms never refresh. Users see nothing happen and click retry repeatedly — each click re-enqueues scrape jobs for every failed platform (report.tsx:121-123 loops all of them), multiplying scrape/LLM cost.
unverified_med_low.fix: Use the shared key factories: `qc.invalidateQueries({ queryKey: reportsKeys.detail(report.id) })` (which also covers the progress sub-key) in both call sites; disable the retry button while pending.

unverified_med_low.title: /scan-report redirect effect missing allReports dependency — bare route wedges on an empty placeholder
unverified_med_low.evidence: scan-report.tsx:230-236: the effect reads `allReports?.[0]` to redirect `/scan-report` → `/scan-report/:id/:lens`, but the dependency array is `[id, lens, navigate]` — `allReports` is omitted. When the reports list resolves after mount (the common case: network fetch), the effect never re-runs.
unverified_med_low.impact: Navigating to /scan-report (a wired route, app.tsx:70) with a cold cache renders the report page with placeholder data (competitorData name "—", scan-report.tsx:375-378) and never redirects to the latest report. Only works when the list happened to be cached at mount. Users land on a dead screen.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add `allReports` to the dependency array (and render a loader while `!id`).

unverified_med_low.title: PDF export poll loop is not cancelled on unmount and keeps polling through errors
unverified_med_low.evidence: scan-report.tsx:188-213: `poll` re-arms itself with `setTimeout(poll, 2500)` for up to 120s; the catch block at 208-210 swallows all errors and continues; there is no cleanup tied to component unmount, and on success line 199 does `window.location.href = ...download` unconditionally.
unverified_med_low.impact: If the user navigates away (or signs out) after starting an export, the orphaned timer keeps hitting /v1/reports/pdf-jobs/:id every 2.5s for up to 2 minutes per click, and a late 'ready' response force-navigates the browser to the download URL from whatever page the user is now on. Multiple clicks stack independent loops (the `exporting` guard state is gone after unmount).
unverified_med_low.fix: Keep the timeout id in a ref cleared by a useEffect cleanup (or use AbortController + a mounted flag), and gate the window.location.href assignment on the component still being mounted.

unverified_med_low.title: Scan submission has no double-click/idempotency protection — duplicate scans double-charge credits
unverified_med_low.evidence: scan.tsx:98-136: the only reentrancy guard is `!isPending` inside `canSubmit` (line 99) and the button's `disabled={!canSubmit}` (line 309). `useMutation().isPending` only flips after React re-renders; two click events dispatched before that re-render (fast double-click/double-tap — note signin.tsx uses the same pattern with an explicit onTouchEnd duplicate handler) both pass the guard and both call `mutateAsync`. No client-generated idempotency key is sent (CreateReportPayload, runScan lines 105-116).
unverified_med_low.impact: Two POST /v1/reports create two reports and, per the credit model (use-reports.ts:142-151, 'server consumed the credit inside the create transaction'), two credit debits and two full scrape+LLM pipeline runs for one user intent — cost amplification and support burden.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add a synchronous ref guard (`if (submittingRef.current) return; submittingRef.current = true`) around start(), and/or send a client idempotency key the API can dedupe on.

unverified_med_low.title: Axios interceptor discards HTTP status; no global 401 handling — expired sessions degrade into silent stale-data mode
unverified_med_low.evidence: axios.ts:10-19 rejects with `error.response.data` only — the status code is thrown away, and there is no 401 → sign-out/redirect handler anywhere (AuthProvider only re-derives state from better-auth's useSession, which is fetched once at mount; auth-provider.tsx:25-45). Query defaults are retry: 0 and refetchOnWindowFocus: false (query-client.ts:13-14), and errored queries keep showing previously cached data.
unverified_med_low.impact: When the better-auth cookie expires mid-session, every subsequent API call 401s but the UI keeps rendering cached report/dashboard data indefinitely (deriveAuthView 'keep' path also deliberately retains the hint for non-401 errors, session-state.ts:27-32 — but nothing ever re-checks the session). Mutations fail with generic messages and components cannot branch on status because it was stripped. Users see stale data and mysterious failures instead of being sent to /signin.
unverified_med_low.fix: Preserve status on the rejected error object and add a response interceptor that, on 401 from API routes, clears the session hint and redirects to /signin (optionally also clearQueryCache).

unverified_med_low.title: Session hint stores user PII in localStorage, contradicting the stated PII policy
unverified_med_low.evidence: session-hint.ts:26-35 writes the full better-auth user object (`storage?.setItem(KEY, JSON.stringify(user))` — includes name, email, image) to localStorage; auth-provider.tsx:49-52 writes it on every session resolution and signin.tsx:87 seeds it with `result.data.user`. Meanwhile app.tsx:92-93 excludes the `me` query from persistence specifically to 'keep PII out of localStorage'.
unverified_med_low.impact: Any XSS or shared-machine access exposes the user's name/email; the hint also survives session expiry (only cleared on definite 401/null — session-state.ts:27-31), so a signed-out-by-expiry browser still displays the previous user's identity and renders the authenticated shell (auth-guard.tsx:35 trusts the hint) until an API call fails.
unverified_med_low.fix: Store only a minimal display token (first name) or nothing; clear the hint whenever a new sign-in begins, and treat hint-derived 'authenticated' as provisional in AuthGuard.

unverified_med_low.title: Inconsistent hardcoded API fallback ports (3001 vs 4000) and duplicate auth clients
unverified_med_low.evidence: scan-report.tsx:176 `const apiBase = () => import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL || "http://localhost:4000"` while global-config.ts:2 and lib/auth.ts:3 fall back to "http://localhost:3001". Additionally two parallel better-auth clients exist: lib/auth-client.ts and lib/auth.ts, both exporting createAuthClient with the same derived baseURL — signin/provider use auth-client.ts, auth.ts is a drifting duplicate.
unverified_med_low.impact: If VITE_API_URL is missing from a production build, the app silently ships pointing at localhost — API calls and, worse, the PDF download redirect (scan-report.tsx:199) go to different dead ports, producing confusing partial failures instead of a build-time error. The duplicate auth client invites future divergence in auth behavior.
unverified_med_low.fix: Fail the build when VITE_API_URL is unset in production (throw in global-config), route all base-URL access through CONFIG.serverUrl, and delete lib/auth.ts in favor of lib/auth-client.ts.

unverified_med_low.title: Competitor avatars fetch from third-party services, leaking scanned competitor names/domains
unverified_med_low.evidence: competitor-avatar.tsx:60-64: after the first-party proxy fails, the component falls back to `https://cdn.brandfetch.io/${d}/w/400/h/400` and `https://www.google.com/s2/favicons?domain=${d}&sz=128`, where `d` derives from user-entered competitor names (resolveDomain, lines 73-82).
unverified_med_low.impact: Every render of a report/list leaks which competitors a customer is researching (plus their IP) to Brandfetch and Google — competitive-intelligence metadata that customers of this product are likely to consider sensitive. Unvalidated `name` is also interpolated into a URL path (encodeURIComponent only on the first source).
unverified_med_low.fix: Serve all logos through the existing /v1/logo proxy (which already exists as source #1) and drop the client-side third-party fallbacks, or make them opt-in.

unverified_med_low.title: emit() pipeline-event insert is not fail-safe and is awaited inside job failure handlers before the status update — a DB blip during failure handling leaves the job locked and masks the original error
unverified_med_low.evidence: emit() does `await db.insert(pipeline_events).values(row);` with no try/catch. Callers await it in catch blocks BEFORE updating job status: source-worker.ts:279 (`await emit({... event: "failed" ...})` precedes the retry/fail UPDATE at :305/:329) and synthesis-worker.ts:283 (precedes UPDATE at :308/:331). It is also awaited as step 1 of processing (source-worker.ts:149, synthesis-worker.ts:79).
unverified_med_low.impact: The most likely reason a job fails is a DB/PgBouncer hiccup — exactly the moment the pipeline_events insert will also fail. When it does, the emit() rejection aborts the catch block: the job's status stays 'running' with a live lock (no retry scheduled, no last_error written) until the stale sweep 25 min (source) or 90 min (synthesis, per config in pg-runner/index.ts:451-452) later, and the log line the poll loop prints is the emit error, not the original scrape/LLM error — the real cause is lost. Same at job start: a failed telemetry insert fails the whole job and burns an attempt.
unverified_med_low.fix: Make emit() swallow-and-log internally (try/catch with pino error, never rethrow) — telemetry writes must never affect job state transitions. Alternatively wrap every emit() call site in try/catch, but fixing it once inside emit() is safer.

unverified_med_low.title: No metrics or alerting layer anywhere: no queue-depth/job-age gauges, no LLM latency/cost metrics, no error tracker — production debugging relies on SSH + PM2 log files and ad-hoc shell scripts
unverified_med_low.evidence: The only operational signal in the entire codebase is the single /health endpoint (server.ts:89-121) exposing one number (oldest_queued_seconds). grep across packages/api/src and packages/worker/src for sentry|prometheus|statsd|datadog|pagerduty|slack|alert returns no monitoring integration (only Razorpay 'webhook' and unrelated matches). Repo root contains check_failed_scan.sh and check_env.sh, and packages/worker/src has poll-report.ts / check-jobs.ts / trigger-fanin.ts — hand tools for SSH-based debugging. Queue depth, jobs-by-status counts, retry rates, fan-in latency, LLM call latency, and per-report token spend exist nowhere as queryable/scrapeable metrics.
unverified_med_low.impact: At thousands of users with spiky load there is no way to answer 'is the queue growing?', 'what is our LLM error rate right now?', or 'did the deploy increase failures?' without SSHing into the single GCE VM and grepping PM2 log files. No alert fires when scans start failing en masse (e.g., OpenRouter outage, Apify credit exhaustion) — discovery is via user complaints. The report_logs/pipeline_events tables enable per-report forensics (good), but there is zero fleet-level or trend visibility and zero paging path.
unverified_med_low.fix: Minimum viable: a /metrics endpoint (or scheduled query) exposing counts by status and age percentiles for report_platform_jobs/synthesis_jobs/report_pdf_jobs, LLM error/latency counters, plus one alerting hook (Slack webhook or UptimeRobot on a 503-capable health route). Adding Sentry to api+worker is a one-day win for exception visibility.

unverified_med_low.title: OpenRouter client retries silently — a 429 storm or provider outage produces zero log lines until jobs exhaust attempts; no LLM call latency measured anywhere; no cost rollup
unverified_med_low.evidence: callWithRetry (lines 118-131) loops up to maxAttempts with `if (!isTransient(err)) throw err; if (attempt < maxAttempts) await sleep(backoffMs(attempt));` — there is no logger in the entire file: no log on 429/5xx/timeout, no attempt number, no latency, no model/status recording. Token usage is returned and logged per stage into report_logs meta (pipeline/run.ts:245, 343) and persisted as columns only for Stage B (source-worker.ts:579-580 prompt_tokens/completion_tokens on report_platform_briefs), but Stage C/D/E usage lands only in report_logs JSON meta and there is no per-report or global cost aggregation.
unverified_med_low.impact: During an OpenRouter degradation, every Stage A batch quietly burns up to 3 attempts x backoff (up to ~90s timeout each) with nothing in the logs; the first visible symptom is source jobs failing 10+ minutes later with a generic message, and diagnosing 'is it us or the provider' requires guesswork. Cost-control: with parallel Stage A batches (50 posts/batch, up to 8 concurrent jobs) there is no way to see spend per report or detect a runaway-cost report/model misconfiguration (e.g., the silent fallback to a rate-limited free model in shared/src/llm/config.ts:19-25 only warns once at boot).
unverified_med_low.fix: Add a pino logger (or injected onRetry/onCall hook) to OpenRouterClient logging attempt, HTTP status, elapsed ms, and model on every retry and final failure; record call latency in the returned LlmResponse; persist stage C/D/E token usage to columns (e.g., on report_pipeline_checkpoints) and expose a per-report token/cost total.

unverified_med_low.title: API handlers map every server-side exception to HTTP 400 and echo raw internal error messages to clients; billing handlers don't log at all
unverified_med_low.evidence: Repeated pattern in ~15 handlers: `} catch (e) { log.error(e); return status(400, { message: "Failed to fetch dashboard", error: e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e) }); }` — same in getProgress.ts:19-25, getMe.ts:19, listEvents.ts:21, addOutreach.ts:31, etc. Billing is worse: verifyPayment.ts:19-23 and createOrder.ts:14 catch WITHOUT any log.error before returning 400.
unverified_med_low.impact: (1) Monitoring blindness: a Postgres outage or code bug surfaces as a wave of 4xx responses, so any error-rate alert keyed on 5xx (the industry default) sees nothing — the API 'never has server errors' by construction. (2) Info leak: raw driver/ORM error strings (connection strings fragments, table/column names, constraint names) are returned to authenticated clients in `error`. (3) Payment verification failures leave no server-side trace at all, compounding the webhook finding.
unverified_med_low.fix: Distinguish expected validation/not-found errors (4xx) from unexpected exceptions (return 500 with a generic message, keep details in the log); add log.error to the billing catches; consider a single Elysia onError hook so severity mapping and logging are consistent instead of copy-pasted.

unverified_med_low.title: Mixed log formats within the same worker process: pino JSON interleaved with hand-rolled console.* lines that carry no timestamp in PM2 log files
unverified_med_low.evidence: logger.ts:14-27 builds a plain string (`[ERROR] stage=... reportId=... msg`) and console.error/warn/log's it, while pg-runner modules use pino JSON (pino({name:"source-worker"}) etc.). More raw console.* in hot paths: recovery.ts:60,73,77,99,121 (`console.log("[recovery] Scanning for stale source jobs...")`), persist.ts:291 (`console.error(`[persist] transaction failed...`)`), scrape/index.ts and synth/index.ts startup lines. ecosystem.config.cjs defines error_file/out_file per app but no log_date_format, so console.* lines land in the PM2 files with no timestamp whatsoever.
unverified_med_low.impact: Post-incident reconstruction on the VM is unreliable: half the lines are JSON with epoch timestamps, half are bare strings with none — you cannot order a `[persist] transaction failed for report X` line relative to the pino lines around it after log rotation/interleaving, and any future log shipper (Loki/CloudWatch) will fail to parse the non-JSON half. Errors also split across -err.log vs -out.log files, fragmenting the timeline further.
unverified_med_low.fix: Route logger.ts's console mirror through a shared pino instance (it already has structured fields — stage/platform/reportId belong in the JSON object, not a joined string); replace remaining console.* in recovery.ts/persist.ts/entrypoints with pino; set log_date_format in ecosystem.config.cjs as a safety net for anything that still writes raw lines.

unverified_med_low.title: Scraper log lines carry no reportId/jobId — with 8 concurrent source jobs, scraper errors cannot be attributed to a scan
unverified_med_low.evidence: Scrapers create module-level loggers with no request context: `const log = pino({ name: "reddit-scraper" })` (reddit/index.ts:9, same in reddit/client.ts:7, reddit/search.ts:5, playstore/client.ts:9); twitter/index.ts:186 and linkedin/index.ts:119 use bare `console.warn(`[twitter] 0 posts for "${competitor}"`)`. The Scraper.fetch() interface receives ScrapeQuery without reportId, and source-worker.ts:363-379 fetchPosts() passes none.
unverified_med_low.impact: WORKER_MAX_CONCURRENT_SOURCE defaults to 8, so up to 8 scrapes interleave in one process's stdout. A reddit-client 429 or auth-failure line can only be tied to a specific report by timestamp proximity, which is ambiguous when two Reddit jobs overlap — debugging 'why did platform X return 0 posts for report Y' requires guessing which log lines belong to Y.
unverified_med_low.fix: Pass reportId (or an opaque correlation id) in ScrapeQuery and have each scraper create a child logger (log.child({ reportId, platform })), or have source-worker wrap scraper output/errors with its own contextual logging.

unverified_med_low.title: Twitter Browserless script swallows per-step navigation failures — silently returns partial data with no failure signal
unverified_med_low.evidence: Inside the injected browser function: reply-fetch loops and whole scrape phases end in `} catch (_) {}` at lines 125, 127, 148, 150 (profile posts + replies, mention search + replies), and the profile-search catch at :103 continues silently. The function then returns whatever accumulated in allPosts.
unverified_med_low.impact: If X changes a selector or the profile phase times out, the scraper returns a reduced (possibly near-empty) post set as if it were a full result — the job 'succeeds', Stage A runs on thin data, and the report quietly degrades. Nobody can tell from logs which scrape phase failed; the only breadcrumb is the post count in the 'Fetched posts' line. This also violates the package rule in packages/scrapers/CLAUDE.md ('Never silently return [] on error').
unverified_med_low.fix: Accumulate per-phase error strings inside the injected function and return them alongside data (`{ data, errors }`); log them (with count of skipped phases) in the scraper and include phase-failure metadata so a systematic selector break is distinguishable from genuinely low activity.

unverified_med_low.title: Log verbosity is hardcoded — no LOG_LEVEL support in any pino instance, so debug logging can't be enabled (or noise reduced) in production without a redeploy
unverified_med_low.evidence: Every pino instance is constructed as `pino({ name: "..." })` with no level option and no process.env.LOG_LEVEL read (pg-runner/index.ts:38, source-worker.ts:41, synthesis-worker.ts:23, pdf-worker.ts:15, events/emit.ts:5, all scraper loggers); grep for LOG_LEVEL across packages returns nothing. The api's elysia-logger config (packages/api/src/config/logger.ts) likewise exposes no level control.
unverified_med_low.impact: During an incident you cannot turn on debug-level detail for the failing component, and during normal high-volume operation you cannot quiet chatty info logs (every job logs ~12 info lines; every /health poll is auto-logged by elysia-logger autoLogging) — log volume and debuggability are both fixed at build time on a single-VM deployment where disk and grep time matter.
unverified_med_low.fix: Create one shared logger factory that reads process.env.LOG_LEVEL (default 'info') and use it everywhere; optionally skip autoLogging for /health to cut probe noise.

unverified_med_low.title: report_logs and pipeline_events grow unboundedly with no retention policy, and /health runs unindexed-looking full-table max() aggregates on every probe
unverified_med_low.evidence: getMostRecentWorkerActivityMs (server.ts:54-80) computes max(locked_at), max(completed_at) over the entire report_platform_jobs and synthesis_jobs tables on every /health request. Worker log() inserts one report_logs row per pipeline log line (logger.ts:30) and emit() one pipeline_events row per stage event (events/emit.ts:29); no code anywhere deletes or archives old rows (no cron, no TTL, no cleanup script in packages/api/src/scripts or packages/worker/src).
unverified_med_low.impact: At thousands of users these tables become the largest in the DB (a single scan writes hundreds of report_logs rows); health probes hitting max() aggregates every few seconds through PgBouncer get progressively slower, and the observability tables themselves start degrading the system they observe. Eventually the /health DB round-trips consume a meaningful share of the 5-connection pool.
unverified_med_low.fix: Add a retention job (delete report_logs/pipeline_events older than N days for completed reports); cache the health queue computation for ~15s in-process; ensure partial indexes exist for the status='queued'/'running' predicates and consider a worker-heartbeat table instead of max() over job tables.
